definition_zh: 空中的；航空的；空气的；（名词）天线
definition_en: relating to the air or to aircraft, or happening high above the ground; as a noun, a device that receives radio or television signals
core_image: 悬在半空的一根细线：既是空气，也是捕捉电波的天线
scene: 清晨的山谷里，摄影师的飞行器缓缓升空，镜头俯瞰着尚未醒来的村庄。The small drone took an aerial photograph of the valley at sunrise.
sceneCN: 这里 aerial 是「空中的、从空中拍摄的」（第 1 个义项：与空气或空中有关）；句意为小型无人机在日出时拍下了山谷的鸟瞰照片。画面中可辨识：飞行器、山谷、晨雾。

collocations.zh: 鸟瞰；从空中看到的景象

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 aerial 加 -ly 构成，义为「在空中；通过航空方式」
由 aerial 加 -ist 构成，指在高空表演的杂技演员，如空中飞人

senses.title: Existing in or relating to the air
senses.titleCN: 空气的；存在于空气中的
senses.definition: relating to the air or existing in it
senses.definitionCN: 与空气有关或存在于空气中的
senses.example: Aerial moisture turned the morning air into a thick mist.
senses.exampleCN: 空气中的水汽让清晨的空气变成了浓雾。
senses.why: Aer is the Greek word for air, and this adjective simply points to that element.
senses.whyCN: aer 是希腊语里表示「空气」的词，这个形容词直接指向这种元素。

senses.title: High above the ground
senses.titleCN: 高悬空中的；在空中发生的
senses.definition: happening or situated high above the ground
senses.definitionCN: 发生在地面上方高处的，或位于高处的
senses.example: An aerial cableway carried the tourists across the gorge.
senses.exampleCN: 一条空中索道把游客送过了峡谷。
senses.why: The same air becomes height: what is aerial is up there, away from the ground.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「空气」义进一步变成高度：aerial 的东西就在上方，远离地面。

senses.title: Done from or by aircraft
senses.titleCN: 航空的；从飞机上进行的
senses.definition: carried out from an aircraft, especially for photography or survey
senses.definitionCN: 从飞机上实施的，尤指摄影或勘测
senses.example: Aerial surveys mapped the damage after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，航空勘测绘制了受灾范围。
senses.why: Once the word moved from air to aircraft, work done in the sky became aerial work.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词从「空气」转向「飞机」，在空中完成的作业就成了 aerial 的工作。

senses.title: A device that receives signals
senses.definition: a metal device, often on a roof, that sends or receives radio and television signals
senses.definitionCN: 常装在屋顶、用于收发广播和电视信号的金属装置
senses.example: He climbed onto the roof to fix the aerial.
senses.exampleCN: 他爬上屋顶去修那根天线。
senses.why: An antenna stands up in the air to catch waves, so English reused the air word for the object itself.
senses.whyCN: 天线竖立在空气中捕捉电波，于是英语干脆用「空气」这个词来称呼这个物件。

senses.title: Growing above the ground: aerial roots
senses.definition: of a plant part, growing above the ground rather than in the soil
senses.definitionCN: 指植物器官长在地面之上而非土壤之中的
senses.example: Orchids use aerial roots to absorb moisture from the humid air.
senses.exampleCN: 兰花用气生根从湿润的空气中吸收水分。
senses.why: Botany keeps the literal sense: the root lives in the air, not in the soil.
senses.whyCN: 植物学保留了最字面的意思：这种根生活在空气里，而不是土壤里。

intro.en: Aerial is built on the Greek word for air and entered English through Latin.
intro.cn: aerial 建立在希腊语表示「空气」的词上，经由拉丁语进入英语。

items.en: The noun aer meant 'air, mist, the lower atmosphere'.
items.cn: 名词 aer 意为「空气、雾气、低层大气」。

items.en: Latin borrowed aer as 'air' and used it in both everyday and scientific writing.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 aer 表示「空气」，日常写作与科学写作中都在使用。

items.en: The adjective aerius meant 'of the air' and supplied the stem behind the English word.
items.cn: 形容词 aerius 意为「空气的」，为英语这个词提供了词干。

items.en: Aerial is recorded in the sixteenth century, first describing things in or of the air.
items.cn: aerial 于十六世纪见于记录，最初描述存在于空气中或与空气有关的事物。

items.en: In the twentieth century the noun aerial was applied to the antenna raised into the air for radio and television.
items.cn: 到了二十世纪，名词 aerial 被用来指为收音机和电视竖在空中的天线。

note.en: The first group gathers words on the same air root or resembling aerial in spelling; the second gathers things that are airborne, overhead, or used to catch signals.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「空气」词根构成的词以及与 aerial 拼写相近的词；第二组收升空的、头顶上的或用于接收信号的事物。

entries.definition: To expose something to air or to force air into it.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使暴露于空气；向……充气」，与 aerial 同出希腊语「空气」词根。

entries.definition: The nest of a bird of prey, built high on a cliff or rock.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「猛禽筑在高处岩壁上的巢」；只是拼写与 aerial 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A performer who works high above the ground, such as a trapeze artist.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指在高空表演的杂技演员，如空中飞人，由 aerial 加 -ist 构成。

entries.definition: Carried in the air, or flying after leaving the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「升空的；在空中的」，强调已经离开地面。

entries.definition: Above a person's head; in the sky directly above.
entries.definitionCN: 副词或形容词，义为「在头顶上方」，只强调相对位置，不涉及航空。

entries.definition: A device that sends or receives radio waves.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「天线」，与 aerial 的名词义项所指同类物件。

normalIntro.en: Aerial can be recalled through its air root, its suffix, and its everyday collocations.
normalIntro.cn: aerial 可以通过「空气」词根、后缀以及常见搭配来记。

normal.en: Aer means air and -ial makes an adjective, so aerial is simply 'of the air'.
normal.cn: aer 意为「空气」，-ial 构成形容词，aerial 就是「空气的」。

normal.en: An aerial view is a view from the air, which fixes the adjective in a familiar phrase.
normal.cn: aerial view 是「从空中看到的景象」，这个常见搭配能固定形容词义。

normal.en: The noun aerial is the antenna that stands up in the air to catch waves.
normal.cn: 名词 aerial 就是竖在空气中捕捉电波的天线。

normal.en: Aerialist adds -ist to the same word and names a person who performs in the air.
normal.cn: aerialist 加 -ist，指在空中表演的人。

normal.en: Aerate and aerobic share the same air root, so the family can be learned together.
normal.cn: aerate 与 aerobic 共享同一「空气」词根，可以整族一起记。

abstract.en: Picture a thin wire hanging above a valley, catching mist on one side and signals on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线悬在山谷上方，一边接住雾气，一边接收信号。

abstract.en: Think of a camera lifting off the ground: the higher it goes, the more the view deserves the name aerial.
abstract.cn: 想象相机离开地面升空：升得越高，眼前的景象越配得上 aerial 这个名字。

abstract.en: Link the word to wind on your face: air is the element behind every sense.
abstract.cn: 把这个词和风吹在脸上的感觉联系起来：空气是它所有义项背后的元素。

examples.en: The drone captured an aerial view of the flooded valley.
examples.cn: 无人机拍下了被洪水淹没的山谷鸟瞰图。

examples.en: He replaced the rusty television aerial on the roof.
examples.cn: 他更换了屋顶上生锈的电视天线。

examples.en: From the ridge, the village looked like a patch of colour in a green sea.
examples.cn: 从山脊望去，村庄像绿色海洋中的一小片色彩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱瑞尔」——爱（ai）上空气，瑞（ri）尔（al）把它挂在高处，正好是悬在半空的细线。

root: 希腊语 aēr（转写为 aer）意为「空气」，拉丁语 aerius 是其形容词形式「空气的」，英语 aerial 由此而来，后缀 -ial 表示「与……有关的」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start from the element air, rise into the sky, move to aircraft, and end with two concrete objects: the antenna and the air root.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从「空气」这一元素出发，升到空中，转向航空，最后落到两个具体物件：天线与气生根。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line suspended in the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一根悬在空中的细线

branches.en: The literal element: what belongs to the air.
branches.cn: 本义：属于空气的事物。

branches.en: Height above the ground, where the air is.
branches.cn: 高度：位于地面之上的空中。

branches.en: Work done from aircraft in the sky.
branches.cn: 从飞机上进行的作业。

branches.en: The antenna that stands in the air to catch waves.
branches.cn: 竖在空气中捕捉电波的天线。

branches.en: The plant root that lives in humid air.
branches.cn: 生长在湿润空气中的植物根。

intro.en: Aerial is built from a Greek air root plus a Latin adjective ending, and its family is easy to map.
intro.cn: aerial 由希腊语「空气」词根加拉丁语形容词词尾构成，词族容易梳理。

latinIntro.en: Latin took aer from Greek and formed aerius 'of the air'; English borrowed the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语从希腊语借入 aer，并构成 aerius「空气的」；英语借用了这个形容词。

latinEntries.example: Aer is the source of the whole family.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aer 是整个词族的来源。

latinEntries.example: Aerius became aerial in English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aerius 在英语中变成了 aerial。

definition_zh: 审美的；美学的；有审美趣味的；（名词）审美观；美学
definition_en: concerned with beauty or the appreciation of beauty; a set of principles about what is beautiful, used as a noun
core_image: 一把衡量美的尺子：看见和谐与愉悦的那双眼睛
scene: 美术馆的展厅里，灯光落在雕塑的弧线上，参观者在一幅画前停了很久。The curator spoke about the aesthetic value of the old woodblock prints.
sceneCN: 这里 aesthetic 是「审美的、美学上的」（第 1 个义项：与美或审美有关）；句意为策展人谈到了那些旧木版画的审美价值。画面中可辨识：展厅、雕塑、画框。

pos.zh: 审美的；美学的；有审美趣味的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加 -ally 构成，义为「在审美方面；从美学上看」
由 aesthetic 加 -ism 构成，指主张「为艺术而艺术」的唯美主义
由 aesthetic 加 -ian 构成，义为「美学家」，也可指美容从业者
由 aesthetic 加 -ize 构成，义为「使具有审美色彩；把……审美化」

senses.title: Connected with beauty
senses.definition: connected with beauty or with the appreciation of beauty
senses.definitionCN: 与美或对美的欣赏有关的
senses.example: The building's aesthetic qualities matter as much as its cost.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑的美学品质与它的造价同样重要。
senses.why: Aisthesis is Greek for perception, and beauty is what the senses single out and enjoy.
senses.whyCN: aisthesis 是希腊语「感知」，而美正是感官挑出来并为之愉悦的东西。

senses.title: Relating to the philosophy of beauty
senses.definition: relating to aesthetics, the branch of philosophy that studies beauty and art
senses.definitionCN: 与美学有关的，即研究美与艺术的哲学分支
senses.example: The paper takes an aesthetic approach to film rather than a political one.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文从美学而非政治的角度研究电影。
senses.why: The same perceptual word was turned into a discipline name in the eighteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表示「感知」的词，在十八世纪被转成了一个学科的名称。

senses.title: Having a refined sense of beauty
senses.definition: showing or having a refined appreciation of beauty, especially in design
senses.definitionCN: 表现出或具有精致的审美鉴赏力，尤指在设计方面
senses.example: Her aesthetic choices are quiet but never dull.
senses.exampleCN: 她的审美选择安静却从不乏味。
senses.why: If perception is trained, the adjective describes the person whose senses are finely tuned to beauty.
senses.whyCN: 如果感知经过训练，这个形容词就用来描述感官对美极为敏锐的人。

senses.title: A personal set of design principles
senses.definition: a set of ideas about what looks beautiful, especially in art, fashion, or design
senses.definitionCN: 关于什么好看的整套观念，尤见于艺术、时尚或设计
senses.example: The studio's aesthetic mixes concrete, glass and warm wood.
senses.exampleCN: 这间工作室的审美风格混合了混凝土、玻璃与暖色木材。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun when we speak of the principles behind a look.
senses.whyCN: 当我们谈论一种外观背后的原则时，形容词就转成了名词。

senses.title: The academic study of beauty
senses.definition: the branch of philosophy that examines beauty, art, and taste, usually written aesthetics
senses.definitionCN: 研究美、艺术与鉴赏力的哲学分支，通常写作 aesthetics
senses.example: Aesthetics asks why a sunset can feel meaningful.
senses.exampleCN: 美学追问：为什么日落会让人觉得有意义。
senses.why: The plural-looking form names a field, just as physics and ethics do.
senses.whyCN: 这个看似复数的形式用来命名一个领域，就像 physics 与 ethics 一样。

intro.en: Aesthetic traces back to a Greek verb of perception and reached English through German philosophy.
intro.cn: aesthetic 可追溯到希腊语表示「感知」的动词，经由德国哲学进入英语。

items.en: Aisthanesthai meant 'to perceive, to feel', and aisthesis was 'perception'.
items.cn: aisthanesthai 意为「感知、感觉」，名词 aisthesis 意为「感知」。

items.en: The adjective aisthetikos described what is perceptive or relates to perception.
items.cn: 形容词 aisthetikos 描述有感知力的或与感知有关的事物。

items.en: Eighteenth-century writers formed aesthetica from the Greek adjective to name a new study of the senses.
items.cn: 十八世纪的写作者用这个希腊形容词构成 aesthetica，为一个研究感官的新学科命名。

items.en: The philosopher Baumgarten is generally credited with founding aesthetics as a separate discipline, and German usage spread the term.
items.cn: 一般认为哲学家鲍姆加登把美学确立为一门独立学科，德语用法把这个术语传播开来。

items.en: English took the adjective first and later used the plural form aesthetics for the discipline.
items.cn: 英语先借入形容词，后来用复数形式 aesthetics 指这门学科。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same perception root; the near-meaning group gathers words about art, taste and elegance.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「感知」词根的一族词；近义组收与艺术、品味、优雅有关的词。

entries.definition: A person who is devoted to beauty and the enjoyment of art.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指热爱美、醉心艺术享受的人，与 aesthetic 同出「感知」词根。

entries.definition: The belief that art should exist for beauty alone, not for moral or social purposes.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指「为艺术而艺术」的唯美主义，由 aesthetic 加 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: A drug that removes feeling or sensation during surgery.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「麻醉剂」；拼写与 aesthetic 相近，但前缀 an- 表示「无」，词源不同。

entries.definition: Having or showing skill and taste in art.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「艺术的；有艺术才华的」，侧重创作能力而非美学理论。

entries.definition: Showing good judgment about what is beautiful or appropriate.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有品味的；雅致的」，侧重选择得体而非学术意义的美。

entries.definition: Graceful and stylish in appearance or manner.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「优雅的；简洁考究的」，侧重外观的精致感。

normalIntro.en: Aesthetic is anchored by the Greek root for perception and by its contrast with anesthetic.
normalIntro.cn: aesthetic 可以靠希腊语「感知」词根，以及它和 anesthetic 的对比来记。

normal.en: Aisth means perceive, so aesthetic is about what the senses notice and value.
normal.cn: aisth 意为「感知」，所以 aesthetic 关乎感官注意到并看重的东西。

normal.en: Anesthetic adds an- 'without' to the same root: without perception, hence numbness.
normal.cn: anesthetic 在同一词根前加 an-「无」：没有感知，也就是麻木。

normal.en: Aesthetic value is a fixed collocation in art writing and anchors the adjective.
normal.cn: aesthetic value 是艺术写作里的固定搭配，可以固定形容词义。

normal.en: An aesthetician is a person who studies or works with beauty.
normal.cn: aesthetician 是研究美或从事美的行业的人。

normal.en: Aesthetics looks plural but names one discipline, like physics.
normal.cn: aesthetics 看着像复数，却和 physics 一样只命名一个学科。

abstract.en: Imagine a ruler that measures not length but harmony.
abstract.cn: 想象一把不量长度、只量和谐的尺子。

abstract.en: Picture a gallery guard who stops you not for touching a painting but for walking past it too fast.
abstract.cn: 想象一位美术馆管理员，不因你触碰画作而拦你，却因你走得太快而拦你。

abstract.en: Think of taste as a muscle: aesthetic is the trained eye that flexes when something is well made.
abstract.cn: 把品味想成一块肌肉：aesthetic 就是看到好作品时会绷紧的那只训练有素的眼睛。

examples.en: The architect cared about aesthetic details as much as about structure.
examples.cn: 这位建筑师对审美细节的在意不亚于对结构的在意。

examples.en: Her aesthetic is simple, warm, and uncluttered.
examples.cn: 她的审美风格简洁、温暖、不杂乱。

examples.en: The hall smelled of fresh paint and old paper.
examples.cn: 大厅里弥漫着新油漆和旧纸张的味道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「爱思塞提克」——爱上思考美感的细节，正好对应这个形容词。

root: 希腊语 aisthanesthai「感知」派生出 aisthētikos「与感知有关的」；十八世纪德国学者把它用于「美学」，英语再借入形容词与学科名。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with perception of beauty, narrows into philosophical theory, then opens into personal taste and the discipline itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从对美的感知出发，收窄为哲学理论，再展开为个人品味与学科本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an eye measuring harmony
core.cn: 核心意象：一只在衡量和谐的眼睛

branches.en: The basic link between the word and beauty.
branches.cn: 这个词与美之间最基本的联系。

branches.en: Beauty turned into an academic question.
branches.cn: 把美变成一个学术问题。

branches.en: A person's trained eye for what looks right.
branches.cn: 个人对好看与否训练有素的眼光。

branches.en: The principles behind a particular look.
branches.cn: 某种外观背后的原则。

branches.en: The discipline that studies beauty and taste.
branches.cn: 研究美与鉴赏力的学科。

intro.en: Aesthetic combines a Greek perception root with adjective and noun endings that also shape its family.
intro.cn: aesthetic 由希腊语「感知」词根与形容词、名词词尾组合而成，这些成分也塑造了它的词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latinized Greek stem aesthetic- became productive in modern European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁化后的希腊词干 aesthetic- 在现代欧洲语言中具有很强的构词能力。

latinEntries.example: Aisthesis is the root of aesthetic.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aisthesis 是 aesthetic 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Aesthetica named the new discipline.
latinEntries.exampleCN: aesthetica 为这门新学科命名。

definition_zh: 事情；事务；事件；（复数）事务；恋情
definition_en: a matter or situation being dealt with; an event; a romantic relationship, especially a secret one; affairs means business or public matters
core_image: 手头正在处理的一桩事：办完才算放下
scene: 清晨的办公室里，秘书把当天的日程摊在桌上，电话一个接一个响起。The diplomat spent the morning handling foreign affairs.
sceneCN: 这里 affairs 是「事务、业务」（第 4 个义项：公共或商务事务）；句意为这位外交官花了一上午处理外交事务。画面中可辨识：办公桌、日程表、电话。

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，义为「事务；业务」，常用于 public affairs、current affairs 等固定说法
复合名词，由 love 与 affair 组成，义为「恋情；风流韵事」
复合名词，义为「外交事务」，指一国与外国的关系

senses.title: A matter being dealt with
senses.definition: a matter, situation, or subject that is being dealt with
senses.definitionCN: 正在处理的事情、情况或议题
senses.example: The repair of the roof turned out to be a complicated affair.
senses.exampleCN: 修屋顶这件事结果变得相当复杂。
senses.why: The Old French source meant 'thing to be done', so an affair is first of all a task on hand.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源意为「有待去做的事」，所以 affair 首先就是手头的一项任务。

senses.title: An event or happening
senses.definition: an event or happening, especially one that attracts attention
senses.definitionCN: 发生的事，尤指引人注意的事件或活动
senses.example: The opening ceremony was a grand affair.
senses.exampleCN: 开幕式是一场盛大的活动。
senses.why: A thing that has been done is also a thing that happened, so the task word slid into the event word.
senses.whyCN: 已经办成的事也是发生过的事，于是「任务」这个词滑向了「事件」。

senses.title: A romantic relationship
senses.definition: a romantic or sexual relationship, especially one that is kept secret
senses.definitionCN: 浪漫或性的关系，尤指隐秘的那种
senses.example: Their affair began during a long business trip.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的恋情始于一次漫长的出差。
senses.why: An affair is something carried on privately, and the phrase came to name a relationship carried on out of sight.
senses.whyCN: affair 是私下进行的事情，这个说法于是用来指背着人进行的关系。

senses.title: Business or public matters
senses.definition: matters of business, government, or public interest, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 商务、政府或公众利益方面的事务，用复数形式
senses.example: She follows current affairs closely.
senses.exampleCN: 她密切关注时事。
senses.why: The plural generalizes the word: many things to do become the whole field of public business.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式把词义一般化：许多要办的事合起来，就成了公共事务这一整个领域。

senses.title: An object or item
senses.definition: an object or item, used informally and now somewhat dated
senses.definitionCN: 物品或东西，用法口语化，如今略显过时
senses.example: He carried a strange little affair made of brass.
senses.exampleCN: 他带着一个黄铜做的小玩意儿，样子很奇怪。
senses.why: In informal speech any thing can be called an affair, because it is simply 'the thing in question'.
senses.whyCN: 在口语里任何东西都能叫 affair，因为它不过是「所说的那件事物」。

intro.en: Affair is a French-shaped word whose core is the Latin verb 'to do'.
intro.cn: affair 是法语形态的词，其核心是拉丁语表示「做」的动词。

items.en: Facere meant 'to do, to make' and supplied the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、制造」，为整个词族提供了动词基础。

items.en: The preposition ad 'to, toward' combined with facere in phrases meaning 'to do to'. Exact classical forms vary.
items.cn: 介词 ad「向、朝」与 facere 组合成表示「对……做」的短语；古典时期的具体形式有差异。

items.en: Old French afaire, literally 'to do', came to mean 'thing to be done, business'.
items.cn: 古法语 afaire 字面是「去做」，后指「有待办的事、事务」。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the fourteenth century with the sense of a matter or business.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入这个词，义为「事情、事务」。

items.en: The romantic sense is recorded later, and the plural affairs settled into public and business usage.
items.cn: 恋情义出现得更晚，复数 affairs 则固定用于公共与商务语境。

note.en: The first group gathers a look-alike and the plural of the same word; the second gathers matters, events and relationship words.
note.cn: 第一组收一个拼写相近的词与本词的复数；第二组收事情、事件与关系类词。

entries.definition: A public fight or noisy disturbance, especially one that involves the law.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「斗殴；扰乱治安」；只是拼写与 affair 相近，来源是古法语表示「惊吓」的词。

entries.definition: The plural of affair, used for business, public matters, or several events.
entries.definitionCN: affair 的复数形式，指业务、公共事务或若干事件。

entries.definition: A subject or situation that is being considered or dealt with.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事情；问题」，最中性，几乎可以替换义项一。

entries.definition: Something that happens, especially something important or planned.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件；活动」，对应义项二，但更强调发生。

entries.definition: An unexpected event, often a minor one or a bad one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「事件；事故」，多指意外或不太愉快的事。

entries.definition: A secret romantic relationship, or a working connection between groups.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「私情」或「联络」，与义项三相近，但更正式。

normalIntro.en: Affair is remembered through the French phrase 'to do' and through its fixed plural phrases.
normalIntro.cn: affair 可以借法语「去做」这一来源，以及几个固定的复数搭配来记。

normal.en: The French source is a phrase meaning 'to do', so an affair is a thing still to be done.
normal.cn: 法语来源是一个表示「去做」的短语，所以 affair 是还有待去办的事。

normal.en: Current affairs are the things being done in the world right now.
normal.cn: current affairs 就是当下世界上正在办的事，也就是时事。

normal.en: Affairs of state are the business of a government.
normal.cn: affairs of state 是政府要办的大事。

normal.en: A love affair is carried on like a private piece of business.
normal.cn: a love affair 像一桩私下的业务一样被经营着。

normal.en: The plural affairs always signals a field of business rather than one single matter.
normal.cn: 复数 affairs 总是表示一整个业务领域，而不是单独一件事。

abstract.en: Picture a desk covered with papers, each one an affair waiting to be finished.
abstract.cn: 想象一张铺满文件的桌子，每一份都是等着被办完的事。

abstract.en: Think of a secret kept in a drawer: that is the affair no one is allowed to see.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉里锁着一个秘密：那就是不许别人看见的私情。

abstract.en: See the word as a container: fill it with tasks, events, or feelings, and it still means 'the thing in hand'.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一个容器：装进任务、事件或感情，它仍然表示「手头那件事」。

examples.en: The whole trip became an expensive affair.
examples.cn: 整趟旅行变成了一件花费高昂的事。

examples.en: She keeps up with current affairs every morning.
examples.cn: 她每天早晨都关注时事。

examples.en: The hallway was quiet after the guests left.
examples.cn: 客人离开后，走廊安静了下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿费尔」——阿（a）费（fei）尔（er）：花一笔费用去办的那件事，就是手头的事务。

root: 古法语 afaire 来自 à faire「去做」，即「有待去做的事」，可追到拉丁语 facere「做、制造」。

sensesIntro.en: One core idea, 'the thing in hand', branches into a task, an event, a private relationship, public business, and even a physical object.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个核心意思「手头那件事」，分出任务、事件、私下关系、公共事务，甚至具体物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the matter in hand
core.cn: 核心意象：手头正在办的那件事

branches.en: The task or matter being handled.
branches.cn: 正在处理的任务或事情。

branches.en: The same thing once it has happened.
branches.cn: 同一件事发生之后的形态，即事件。

branches.en: A relationship carried on privately.
branches.cn: 私下进行的一段关系。

branches.en: Many matters gathered into a field of business.
branches.cn: 许多事汇成一个业务领域。

branches.en: Any object referred to informally as 'the thing'.
branches.cn: 口语中笼统指称的「那个东西」。

intro.en: Affair is mostly a whole borrowed word, but its Latin pieces still explain related forms.
intro.cn: affair 基本是整体借入的词，但其中的拉丁成分仍能解释相关形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb facere and the prefix ad- underlie the French phrase from which affair came.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 facere 与前缀 ad- 构成了 affair 所来自的那个法语短语。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

items.example: Facere is the source of many English words.
items.exampleCN: facere 是许多英语词的来源。

items.example: The phrase became afaire in Old French.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语在古法语中变成 afaire。

latinEntries.example: Afaire entered English as affair.
latinEntries.exampleCN: afaire 进入英语后写作 affair。

latinEntries.example: Facere lies behind the phrase a faire.
latinEntries.exampleCN: facere 藏在短语 a faire 背后。

definition_zh: 影响；感动；（疾病）侵袭；假装；喜欢
definition_en: to produce a change in someone or something; to move the emotions; to attack as a disease does; to pretend to feel or have something
core_image: 一只手伸过去，改变了原来的样子：影响、触动、侵袭
scene: 暴雨连续下了几天，河水漫过堤岸，低处的农田最先遭了殃。The flood affected thousands of families along the river.
sceneCN: 这里 affected 是「影响了、波及了」（第 1 个义项：对某人某物产生作用）；句意为洪水波及了河边的数千个家庭。画面中可辨识：暴雨、漫水的河堤、农田。

pos.zh: 影响；感动；（疾病）侵袭；假装；喜欢

derivatives.zh: 由过去分词转化而来，义为「受影响的」，也可指「做作的」
由现在分词转化而来，义为「动人的；令人感伤的」
由 affect 加 -ion 构成，义为「喜爱；感情」
由 affected 加 -ly 构成，义为「做作地；装模作样地」
由 dis- 加 affected 构成，义为「不满的；不忠的」
由 un- 加 affected 构成，义为「未受影响的；自然的」

senses.title: To produce a change in something
senses.definition: to produce a change in a person, thing, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 对人、事物或局面产生改变
senses.example: Rising sea levels affect coastal cities.
senses.exampleCN: 海平面上升影响着沿海城市。
senses.why: Afficere meant to act upon something, and the modern verb keeps that image of one thing working on another.
senses.whyCN: afficere 意为「对某物施加作用」，现代动词保留了甲作用于乙这一意象。

senses.title: To move the emotions
senses.definition: to cause a strong emotional response in someone
senses.definitionCN: 在某人心中引起强烈的情感反应
senses.example: Her letter affected him more than he expected.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信对他的触动比他预想的更深。
senses.why: The heart can be acted upon as well as a body, so the doing word became a feeling word.
senses.whyCN: 心也可以像身体一样被施加作用，于是这个「做」的词变成了「感」的词。

senses.title: To attack as a disease does
senses.definition: of a disease or condition, to attack or harm a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或病症侵袭、损害身体某部位
senses.example: The virus can affect the lungs and the nervous system.
senses.exampleCN: 这种病毒可能侵袭肺部和神经系统。
senses.why: An illness acts upon the body without invitation, which is the oldest sense of the Latin verb.
senses.whyCN: 疾病不请自来地作用于身体，这正是拉丁语动词最古老的义项。

senses.title: To pretend to feel or have
senses.definition: to pretend to have a feeling, attitude, or quality
senses.definitionCN: 假装具有某种感情、态度或特质
senses.example: He affected indifference when he heard the news.
senses.exampleCN: 听到这个消息时，他假装冷漠。
senses.why: To affect something is to put it on as a mask, so the verb also means to display a feeling you do not have.
senses.whyCN: affect 某物就像戴上一副面具，于是这个动词也指表现出并非真实的情感。

senses.title: To be fond of, in formal use
senses.definition: to like or be fond of something, used in formal or literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 喜欢或偏爱某事物，用于正式或文学写作
senses.example: The poet affected the company of quiet scholars.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人喜欢与安静学者为伴。
senses.why: This favourable sense grew beside the pretence sense, since what you choose to display can also be what you love.
senses.whyCN: 这个表示偏爱的义项与「假装」义并行发展，因为你选择展示的东西也可以是所爱之物。

intro.en: Affect comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to do something to', built from a prefix and the verb 'to do'.
intro.cn: affect 来自拉丁语动词「对……做点什么」，由一个前缀和「做」这个动词构成。

items.en: Afficere meant 'to do something to, to act upon, to treat'.
items.cn: afficere 意为「对……做点什么、施加作用、对待」。

items.en: The prefix ad- 'to, toward' is assimilated to af- before f, giving the shape the English word keeps.
items.cn: 前缀 ad-「向、朝」在 f 前同化为 af-，英语词保留了这一形状。

items.en: Facere 'to do, make' is the second element, so the verb literally means 'to do to'.
items.cn: 第二个成分是 facere「做、制造」，所以这个动词字面就是「对……做」。

items.en: Old French affecter carried the word into English with senses of aiming at and pretending.
items.cn: 古法语 affecter 把这个词带入英语，带有「追求」与「装作」的意思。

items.en: The emotional and medical senses are recorded later, while the pretence sense was already established.
items.cn: 情感义与医学义出现得更晚，而「假装」义当时已经确立。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same 'do to' verb; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of influence and emotional change.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「对……做」动词构成的一族词；近义组收表示影响与情感变化的动词。

entries.definition: Behaviour or speech that is deliberately unnatural in order to impress others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「做作；装腔作势」，由 affect 的「假装」义加 -ation 构成。

entries.definition: Influenced by something, or artificial in manner.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受影响的」或「做作的」，由 affect 的过去分词转化而来。

entries.definition: A feeling of fondness or tender attachment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喜爱；感情」，与 affect 同源但词义已明显分化。

entries.definition: To have an effect on how something develops or behaves.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「影响」，侧重对发展或行为的作用，语气比 affect 更中性。

entries.definition: To cause someone to feel strong emotion, especially sympathy or sadness.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使感动」，对应义项二，多指引起同情或悲伤。

entries.definition: To influence someone's opinion or decision.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「左右；动摇」，侧重影响判断与决定，而非客观状态。

normalIntro.en: Affect is best remembered as 'do to': the prefix ad- plus the verb 'to do'.
normalIntro.cn: affect 最好记成「对……做」：前缀 ad- 加上表示「做」的动词。

normal.en: Ad- means to and facere means do, so affect is to do something to someone.
normal.cn: ad- 意为「向」，facere 意为「做」，所以 affect 就是对某人做点什么。

normal.en: Be affected by something is the passive shape you will meet most often.
normal.cn: be affected by 是它最常见的被动形式，遇到就该认出。「be affected by」

normal.en: Affection is the same family, but it settled on the feeling rather than the action.
normal.cn: affection 同属一族，但它落在感情而不是动作上。

normal.en: Affected can mean influenced or artificial, and the second sense links to affectation.
normal.cn: affected 既可指「受影响的」，也可指「做作的」，后一义与 affectation 相连。

normal.en: Affecting is the adjective for something that moves you.
normal.cn: affecting 是形容让人动容之物的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing into soft clay: the mark left behind is the effect of having affected it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按进柔软的黏土：留下的印子就是 affect 之后的效果。

abstract.en: See a disease as an uninvited hand that reaches into the body.
abstract.cn: 把疾病看成一只不请自来的手，伸进了身体里。

abstract.en: Think of a mask: to affect indifference is to wear calmness you do not feel.
abstract.cn: 想象一副面具：affect indifference 就是戴上并不真有的平静。

examples.en: Rising sea levels affect coastal cities.
examples.cn: 海平面上升影响着沿海城市。

examples.en: Her letter affected him more than he expected.
examples.cn: 她的信对他的触动比他预想的更深。

examples.en: The meeting ended earlier than planned.
examples.cn: 会议比计划结束得更早。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿费克特」——阿（a）费（fei）克（ke）特（te），花了力气去对别人「施加影响」。

root: 拉丁语 afficere「对……做点什么」，由 ad-「向」加 facere「做」构成；古法语 affecter 把它带入英语。

sensesIntro.en: From acting upon a thing, the verb spreads to acting on feelings, on the body, and finally to putting on a feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: 从作用于事物出发，这个动词扩展到作用于情感、作用于身体，最后变成「戴上一副情感」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching out and changing what it touches
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸过去，改变了所触之物

branches.en: Acting upon a thing so that it changes.
branches.cn: 作用于事物使其改变。

branches.en: The same action aimed at the emotions.
branches.cn: 同一作用指向情感。

branches.en: An illness acting on the body.
branches.cn: 疾病对身体的作用。

branches.en: Putting on a feeling as a mask.
branches.cn: 像戴面具一样装出某种情感。

branches.en: Choosing to favour something in formal style.
branches.cn: 在书面语中选择偏爱某物。

intro.en: Affect is a transparent Latin construction, and its affixes also build a large word family.
intro.cn: affect 是结构透明的拉丁语构词，其中的词缀还构成了一个很大的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus facere produced afficere; the assimilated af- is the form English inherited.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 facere 构成 afficere；英语继承的是同化后的 af- 形式。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Afficere is the direct source of affect.
latinEntries.exampleCN: afficere 是 affect 的直接来源。

latinEntries.example: Affectare fed the sense of pretence.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affectare 促成了「假装」这一义项。

definition_zh: 喜爱；钟爱；感情；（医学旧义）疾患
definition_en: a feeling of fondness or tender attachment; in older medical use, a disease or condition of the body or mind
core_image: 心里向某个人轻轻倾过去的一股暖流
scene: 冬夜的厨房里，母亲把一碗热汤推到孩子面前，看着他喝下第一口。The old dog followed him everywhere with obvious affection.
sceneCN: 这里 affection 是「喜爱、深情」（第 1 个义项：对人或动物的钟爱）；句意为那只老狗带着明显的依恋，走到哪里都跟着他。画面中可辨识：热汤、厨房、老狗。

pos.zh: 喜爱；钟爱；感情；（医学旧义）疾患

derivatives.zh: 由 affection 加 -ate 构成，义为「深情的；充满爱意的」
由 affectionate 加 -ly 构成，义为「深情地；亲昵地」
由 affection 加 -al 构成，义为「情感的；感情方面的」，多用于心理学
由 dis- 加 affection 构成，义为「不满；疏离感」

senses.title: A feeling of fondness
senses.definition: a feeling of fondness or liking for a person, animal, or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对人、动物或事物怀有的喜爱或好感
senses.example: She looked at the old photographs with affection.
senses.exampleCN: 她满怀深情地看着那些旧照片。
senses.why: The Latin source named a state of being moved, and the feeling that stays is fondness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源指一种被触动的状态，而留下来最久的那种感受就是喜爱。

senses.title: Tender attachment between people
senses.definition: a tender attachment or warm feeling between people, often shown in small acts
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间温柔的情感或依恋，常通过小动作表现出来
senses.example: His affection for his sister showed in the way he saved her the last piece.
senses.exampleCN: 他对妹妹的感情体现在把最后一块留给了她。
senses.why: Fondness grown strong and steady becomes attachment, the warmth that binds two people.
senses.whyCN: 喜爱变得强烈而稳定，就成了依恋，也就是把两个人连在一起的温度。

senses.title: Feelings in the plural
senses.definition: feelings or emotions, especially warm ones, used in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 各种感情或情绪，尤指温暖的情感，多用复数
senses.example: He hid his affections behind a joking manner.
senses.exampleCN: 他用开玩笑的样子掩饰自己的情感。
senses.why: The plural spreads one feeling into a whole inner life, the many attachments a person carries.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式把一种感情铺展成整个内心世界，即一个人携带的许多牵挂。

senses.title: A bodily or mental condition, in old medicine
senses.definition: a disease or abnormal condition of the body or mind, a sense now largely historical
senses.definitionCN: 身体或精神的疾病、异常状态，这一义项如今基本成为历史用法
senses.example: The old medical text lists several affections of the lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧医书列出了几种肺部疾患。
senses.why: A disease was seen as something acting on the body, so the word for being affected also named the illness itself.
senses.whyCN: 疾病被看作作用于身体的东西，于是「被作用」这个词也用来指疾病本身。

intro.en: Affection is the noun built on the Latin verb 'to act upon', and its medical sense is much older than its romantic one.
intro.cn: affection 是在拉丁语动词「施加作用」基础上构成的名词，它的医学义比情感义古老得多。

items.en: Afficere meant 'to do something to, to affect', built from ad- and facere.
items.cn: afficere 意为「对……做点什么、施加影响」，由 ad- 与 facere 构成。

items.en: Affectio named a state or disposition produced in someone, whether of body or of mind.
items.cn: affectio 指在某人身上产生的状态或倾向，既可以是身体的，也可以是心理的。

items.en: Old French took the word in the sense of a disposition or feeling and passed it to English.
items.cn: 古法语以「性情、感受」之义接受这个词，并把它传给英语。

items.en: Early English used affection for a state of body or mind as well as for an emotional disposition.
items.cn: 早期英语里，affection 既指身心状态，也指情感倾向。

items.en: The medical sense faded while the sense of fondness became dominant, and affectionate was formed from the noun.
items.cn: 医学义逐渐消退，喜爱义成为主流，形容词 affectionate 则由这个名词构成。

note.en: The first group gathers words from the same affect root; the second gathers feelings of liking and attachment.
note.cn: 第一组收同一 affect 词根的一族词；第二组收表示喜欢与依恋的情感词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to influence or to move emotionally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「影响；使感动」，是 affection 的动词同源词，词性不同。

entries.definition: Deliberately unnatural behaviour meant to impress others.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「做作；装腔作势」，与 affection 同源但意义偏负面。

entries.definition: Showing warmth and fondness openly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「深情的；充满爱意的」，直接由 affection 派生。

entries.definition: A feeling of liking or love for someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「喜爱；钟情」，与义项一几乎同义，但更口语。

entries.definition: A strong feeling of deep affection for another person.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「爱」，情感强度高于 affection，常指更深的爱。

entries.definition: A feeling of being emotionally connected to someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「依恋」，强调情感上的联结，与义项二相近。

entries.definition: A friendly and affectionate quality in a person or behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「温情；亲切」，侧重待人的温暖态度。

normalIntro.en: Affection is the noun of affect, and its family shows how an action turns into a feeling.
normalIntro.cn: affection 是 affect 的名词形式，它的词族展示了动作如何变成情感。

normal.en: Affect means to act upon or move, and -ion turns that action into a state of feeling.
normal.cn: affect 意为作用于或触动，-ion 把这个动作变成一种情感状态。

normal.en: To be affected by someone is to be moved by them, and affection is the warmth left behind.
normal.cn: 被某人 affect，就是被其触动，而 affection 是留下的那份暖意。

normal.en: Affectionate adds -ate to the noun and describes someone who shows the feeling openly.
normal.cn: affectionate 在名词后加 -ate，形容把这种感情明显表现出来的人。

normal.en: A public display of affection is the full phrase behind the everyday abbreviation PDA.
normal.cn: 「public display of affection」是日常缩写 PDA 背后的完整说法。

normal.en: The old medical sense survives in phrases about an affection of the lungs or nerves.
normal.cn: 旧的医学义还残留在表示肺部或神经疾患的短语里。

abstract.en: Picture a warm current leaning toward one person and never reaching anyone else.
abstract.cn: 想象一股暖流只向某一个人倾斜，从不流向别人。

abstract.en: Think of a hand kept on a shoulder for one extra second: that second is affection.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在肩上多停留了一秒：那一秒就是 affection。

abstract.en: See the word as the soft afterglow of an action that once moved you.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一次触动之后留下的柔光。

examples.en: She spoke of her old teacher with great affection.
examples.cn: 她满怀深情地谈起自己的旧日老师。

examples.en: The child showed affection by clinging to his father's coat.
examples.cn: 孩子抓着父亲的外套，用这种方式表达依恋。

examples.en: The kitchen was warm and smelled of ginger.
examples.cn: 厨房很暖，飘着姜的味道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿费克心」——阿（a）费（fei）克（ke）心（xin），费了心思去喜欢一个人。

root: 拉丁语 afficere「对……施加作用」派生出 affectio「被作用的状态、性情」，古法语带入英语后逐渐专指「喜爱」。

sensesIntro.en: The noun starts as any state produced in a person, narrows into fondness, and widens again in the plural to a whole emotional life.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词起初指人身上产生的任何状态，后收窄为喜爱，又在复数中扩展为整个情感生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm current leaning toward one person
core.cn: 核心意象：一股只向某个人倾斜的暖流

branches.en: The basic feeling of liking.
branches.cn: 最基本的喜欢之情。

branches.en: Fondness grown into attachment between people.
branches.cn: 喜爱成长为人与人之间的依恋。

branches.en: The plural opens the feeling into a whole inner life.
branches.cn: 复数把这种感情展开为整个内心世界。

branches.en: The old sense of a condition acting on body or mind.
branches.cn: 作用于身心的状态这一古老义项。

branches.en: Liking and attachment as one continuous line.
branches.cn: 喜爱与依恋构成一条连续的线。

intro.en: Affection is built from Latin pieces that also explain its adjective and its negative twin.
intro.cn: affection 由拉丁语成分构成，这些成分也解释了它的形容词与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin afficere and its noun affectio supply the stem; English added its own endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 afficere 及其名词 affectio 提供了词干，英语再加上自己的词尾。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Afficere stands behind affection.
latinEntries.exampleCN: afficere 是 affection 背后的动词。

latinEntries.example: Affectio passed through French into English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affectio 经由法语进入英语。

definition_zh: 使隶属；使加入；加入；附属机构
definition_en: to officially join or connect an organization with a larger one; a company or group that is linked to a larger organization
core_image: 一根细枝接到主干上：小机构挂进大体系
scene: 城市的街角，几个独立的小工作室共用一块招牌，也共用同一套培训。The small studio chose to affiliate with a national network.
sceneCN: 这里 affiliate 是「加入、隶属」（第 1 个义项：正式加入一个更大的组织）；句意为这家小工作室选择加入一个全国性的网络。画面中可辨识：共用招牌、工作室、培训手册。

derivatives.zh: 由 affiliate 加 -ion 构成，义为「隶属关系；加入；归属」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「附属的；有关联的」
由 dis- 加 affiliate 构成，义为「退出；脱离隶属关系」

senses.title: To connect an organization with a larger one
senses.definition: to officially attach a person or organization to a larger group
senses.definitionCN: 正式把个人或组织附属于一个更大的团体
senses.example: The clinic agreed to affiliate itself with the university hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所同意隶属于那所大学医院。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to adopt as a son, so the modern sense keeps the image of taking a smaller unit into a family.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「收为养子」，现代义保留了把较小单位收进一个家族的形象。

senses.title: To join or become linked
senses.definition: to join a larger group or form a working link with it, used without an object
senses.definitionCN: 加入一个更大的团体或与其建立工作联系，作不及物动词
senses.example: Several local clubs affiliate with the national association each year.
senses.exampleCN: 每年都有几个本地俱乐部加入这个全国协会。
senses.why: Once the smaller unit can act for itself, the verb turns intransitive: it chooses to join.
senses.whyCN: 当较小单位能自行行动时，这个动词就转为不及物：它自己选择加入。

senses.title: A linked organization
senses.definition: a company, club, or group that is officially connected to a larger organization
senses.definitionCN: 正式与更大组织相连的公司、俱乐部或团体
senses.example: The radio station is a local affiliate of the national network.
senses.exampleCN: 这家电台是该全国网络的本地附属台。
senses.why: The verb's object becomes a noun: the unit that has been taken into the family.
senses.whyCN: 动词的宾语转成名词：那个被收进家族的单位。

senses.title: To establish a legal link of parentage
senses.definition: in law, to establish the legal relationship of a child to a parent, or to assign something to a source
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上确立子女与父母之间的亲子关系，或把某物归属于某一来源
senses.example: The court affiliated the child to the man named in the will.
senses.exampleCN: 法院认定这个孩子与遗嘱中所写的那名男子存在父子关系。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense surviving almost unchanged: to declare that someone belongs to a particular father.
senses.whyCN: 这是几乎原样保留的最古老义项：宣告某人属于某位父亲。

intro.en: Affiliate began as a legal word about sons and only later became a word about organizations.
intro.cn: affiliate 起初是关于儿子的法律词，后来才变成关于组织的词。

items.en: Filius meant 'son', and the whole family of the word grows from that single noun.
items.cn: filius 意为「儿子」，整个词族都从这个名词生长出来。

items.en: Affiliare meant 'to adopt as a son', formed with ad- 'to' and filius.
items.cn: affiliare 意为「收为养子」，由 ad-「向」与 filius 构成。

items.en: Medieval legal Latin used affiliatus for a child legally assigned to a father.
items.cn: 中世纪法律拉丁语用 affiliatus 指在法律上归属于某位父亲的孩子。

items.en: English extended the word from family law to the joining of societies and institutions.
items.cn: 英语把这个词从家庭法扩展到社团与机构的加入。

items.en: Business and media gave the noun affiliate its everyday sense of a linked local branch.
items.cn: 商业与传媒赋予名词 affiliate 今天的日常义：有关联的本地分支。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin 'son' root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs and nouns of joining and attachment.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语「儿子」词根的一族词；近义组收表示加入与附属的动词和名词。

entries.definition: The state of being officially connected to a larger group.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「隶属关系；归属」，由 affiliate 加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: Officially connected with or controlled by a larger organization.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「附属的；有关联的」，是 affiliate 的过去分词。

entries.definition: Relating to a son or daughter and the duty owed to parents.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「子女的；孝顺的」，与 affiliate 同出拉丁语 filius「儿子」。

entries.definition: To join or fasten one thing to another.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「附上；连接」，可指物理连接，也可指关系上的归属。

entries.definition: To connect people or organizations in a working relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使联合；使关联」，语气比 affiliate 更宽泛。

entries.definition: To become a member of a group or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「加入」，最通用，不强调大小机构之间的隶属。

entries.definition: A company owned or controlled by a larger company.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「子公司；附属公司」，与义项三相近，但强调所有权。

normalIntro.en: Affiliate is anchored by the Latin word for son and by the modern image of a branch joining a tree.
normalIntro.cn: affiliate 可以靠拉丁语「儿子」这个词，以及树枝接到树干上的现代意象来记。

normal.en: Filius means son, so affiliate first meant to adopt as a son.
normal.cn: filius 意为「儿子」，所以 affiliate 最初指「收为养子」。

normal.en: An affiliate is a unit taken into a larger family and given its name.
normal.cn: affiliate 就是被收进更大体系并挂上其名号的单位。

normal.en: Be affiliated with is the phrase you will see in forms and official descriptions.
normal.cn: be affiliated with 是表格和官方介绍里常见的说法。

normal.en: Affiliation is the noun for the link itself, not for the unit.
normal.cn: affiliation 指联系本身，而不是那个单位。

normal.en: Disaffiliate is its opposite: to leave the family.
normal.cn: disaffiliate 是它的反义：离开这个家族。

abstract.en: Picture a small branch grafted onto a strong trunk, keeping its own leaves but sharing the root.
abstract.cn: 想象一根小枝嫁接到粗壮的树干上，保留自己的叶子，却共享同一个根。

abstract.en: Think of a local radio station carrying a national logo on its sign.
abstract.cn: 想象一家本地电台在招牌上挂着全国网络的标志。

abstract.en: See the word as a door: joining means walking through it and taking the larger house's name.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一扇门：加入就是走进去，并冠上大房子的姓氏。

examples.en: The research centre is affiliated with a major university.
examples.cn: 这个研究中心隶属于一所重点大学。

examples.en: The local newspaper became an affiliate of the national chain.
examples.cn: 这家本地报纸成了全国报业连锁的附属机构。

examples.en: Members voted to leave the association last spring.
examples.cn: 成员们在去年春天投票决定退出该协会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿菲利特」——阿（a）菲（fei）利（li）特（te），小机构特别想依附大网络。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 filius「儿子」构成 affiliare「收为养子」，中世纪法律拉丁语 affiliatus 指法律上归属某位父亲的孩子；作名词时读「/əˈfɪliət/」。

sensesIntro.en: The word travels from family law to institutional life: adopt a son, join a group, become a branch, and finally declare a legal parent.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从家庭法走到机构生活：收为养子、加入团体、成为分支，最后仍保留宣告法律父关系的一义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branch grafted onto a trunk
core.cn: 核心意象：一根嫁接到树干上的枝条

branches.en: A larger body takes a smaller one into its family.
branches.cn: 较大机构把较小单位收进自己的家族。

branches.en: The smaller unit chooses to join on its own.
branches.cn: 较小单位自行选择加入。

branches.en: The joined unit itself, now a named branch.
branches.cn: 被收进的单位本身，如今是有名号的分支。

branches.en: The oldest legal sense: declaring a parental link.
branches.cn: 最古老的法律义：宣告亲子关系。

branches.en: Attachment seen from the larger and the smaller side.
branches.cn: 从大机构与小机构两个视角看同一种附属关系。

intro.en: Affiliate is a Latin legal construction whose parts still explain affiliation and filial.
intro.cn: affiliate 是拉丁语法律构词，其成分仍能解释 affiliation 与 filial。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus filius produced affiliare; the noun filius also gave English filial.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 filius 构成 affiliare；名词 filius 还给了英语 filial。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Filius is the root of affiliate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: filius 是 affiliate 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Affiliare entered law and then business.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affiliare 先进入法律，后进入商业。

definition_zh: 断言；肯定；证实；（法律）维持原判
definition_en: to state something firmly as true; to confirm or support a claim; in law, to uphold a judgment
core_image: 把一件事按实、按稳地放在桌上，说「就是这样」
scene: 法庭的木槌还未落下，证人把手放在栏杆上，又重复了一遍自己的说法。She affirmed that the signature was hers.
sceneCN: 这里 affirmed 是「断言、郑重声明」（第 1 个义项：坚定地声明某事为真）；句意为她断言那个签名是自己的。画面中可辨识：证人席、栏杆、木槌。

pos.zh: 断言；肯定；证实；（法律）维持原判

derivatives.zh: 由 affirm 加 -ation 构成，义为「断言；肯定；确认」
由 affirm 加 -ative 构成，义为「肯定的；赞成的」，也可作名词指肯定回答
由 affirmative 加 -ly 构成，义为「肯定地；赞许地」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「已确认的；被维持的」

senses.title: To state firmly that something is true
senses.definition: to state something firmly and confidently as true
senses.definitionCN: 坚定而自信地声明某事为真
senses.example: She affirmed that the signature was hers.
senses.exampleCN: 她断言那个签名是自己的。
senses.why: Firmus means firm, and affirmare means to make firm, so affirming is planting a statement so it cannot wobble.
senses.whyCN: firmus 意为「稳固」，affirmare 意为「使稳固」，所以 affirm 就是把一句话钉稳，让它不再摇晃。

senses.title: To confirm or ratify
senses.definition: to confirm that something is true or valid, often in an official setting
senses.definitionCN: 确认某事为真或有效，常用于正式场合
senses.example: The committee affirmed the findings of the earlier report.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会确认了早先那份报告的结论。
senses.why: What has been made firm can also be made official: confirmation is the public version of the same act.
senses.whyCN: 被钉稳的东西也可以被正式化：确认就是同一动作的公开版本。

senses.title: To support or defend a value
senses.definition: to express support for a principle, value, or position
senses.definitionCN: 对某项原则、价值或立场表示支持
senses.example: The speech affirmed the importance of free inquiry.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇演讲强调了自由探究的重要性。
senses.why: To affirm a value is to hold it firm against doubt, giving it the strength of a stated principle.
senses.whyCN: 肯定一种价值，就是在怀疑面前把它握稳，赋予它一条明确原则的力量。

senses.title: To uphold a court ruling
senses.definition: in law, of a higher court, to declare that a lower court's judgment stands
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上，上级法院宣布下级法院的判决继续有效
senses.example: The appeal court affirmed the original verdict.
senses.exampleCN: 上诉法院维持了原判。
senses.why: The judicial sense is the literal one: the ruling is made firm again by a higher authority.
senses.whyCN: 司法义是最字面的：判决被更高一级的权威重新钉稳。

intro.en: Affirm is built on the Latin adjective for 'firm', and its legal sense is close to the original image.
intro.cn: affirm 建立在拉丁语表示「稳固」的形容词上，其法律义最接近原始意象。

items.en: Firmus meant 'firm, strong, steady', and it also gave English firm.
items.cn: firmus 意为「稳固、强壮、坚定」，它也给了英语 firm 这个词。

items.en: Affirmare meant 'to make firm, strengthen, assert', built with ad- and firmus.
items.cn: affirmare 意为「使稳固、加强、断言」，由 ad- 与 firmus 构成。

items.en: Old French passed the verb to English with the sense of asserting or maintaining.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词传给英语，带有「断言、坚持」的意思。

items.en: The verb is recorded in the fourteenth century in both statement and legal use.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四世纪已有记录，既用于一般陈述，也用于法律。

items.en: Affirmation and affirmative grew into everyday words for agreement and positive response.
items.cn: affirmation 与 affirmative 发展为日常表示同意与肯定回答的词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same 'firm' root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of asserting, confirming, and upholding.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「稳固」词根的一族词；近义组收断言、确认与维持类的动词。

entries.definition: A firm statement that something is true, or a positive declaration.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「断言；肯定」，由 affirm 加 -ation 构成。

entries.definition: Expressing agreement or a positive answer.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「肯定的；赞成的」，也可作名词指肯定回答。

entries.definition: Solid, steady, and not likely to move or change.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「稳固的；坚定的」，是 affirm 所依托的拉丁形容词在英语中的直系形式。

entries.definition: To state something confidently, often without providing proof.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「断言；声称」，语气强硬，但不一定给出证据。

entries.definition: To show or state that something is true or correct.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证实；确认」，强调用证据或权威使某事确定。

entries.definition: To announce something officially or formally.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣布；声明」，侧重公开与正式。

entries.definition: To support a law or decision and declare it still valid.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「维持；支持」，与义项四的法律用法最接近。

normalIntro.en: Affirm is remembered through the word firm: to affirm is to make a statement firm.
normalIntro.cn: affirm 可以借 firm 这个词来记：affirm 就是把一句话说得稳稳的。

normal.en: Firmus means firm, and affirmare means to make firm, so affirm is to steady a claim.
normal.cn: firmus 意为「稳固」，affirmare 意为「使稳固」，所以 affirm 就是把主张稳住。

normal.en: Affirmation is the noun, and affirmative is the adjective for a positive answer.
normal.cn: affirmation 是名词，affirmative 是表示肯定回答的形容词。

normal.en: An appeal court affirms a verdict, which means it makes the ruling stand.
normal.cn: 上诉法院 affirm 一项裁决，意思是让判决继续有效。

normal.en: Affirmative action is a fixed phrase about policies that support a group.
normal.cn: 「affirmative action」是表示支持某群体的政策的固定说法。

normal.en: Affirm is stronger than say and more formal than agree.
normal.cn: affirm 比 say 更强，也比 agree 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pressing a sheet of paper flat so the wind cannot lift it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一张纸压平，让风无法把它掀起。

abstract.en: Think of a judge's gavel coming down: the sound makes the decision firm.
abstract.cn: 想象法官的木槌落下：那一声让决定变得稳固。

abstract.en: See the word as a nail driven into wood: once in, the claim stays put.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一枚钉进木头的钉子：一旦钉入，主张就不动了。

examples.en: The witness affirmed that she had seen the car leave.
examples.cn: 证人断言自己看见那辆车离开。

examples.en: The court affirmed the earlier ruling on appeal.
examples.cn: 法院在上诉中维持了先前的裁决。

examples.en: The room fell silent as the clerk read the document.
examples.cn: 书记员宣读文件时，房间安静了下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿飞尔姆」——阿（a）飞（fei）尔（er）姆（mu），把一句话钉得稳稳的，不让它晃动。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 firmus「稳固」构成 affirmare「使稳固、断言」，古法语传入英语后保留「断言」与「维持判决」两条线。

sensesIntro.en: All senses keep the same image: a statement or decision is made firm, whether by words, by authority, or by a higher court.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都保留同一意象：一句话或一项决定被钉稳，无论靠言辞、靠权威，还是靠上级法院。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a claim pressed firmly onto the table
core.cn: 核心意象：把一项主张稳稳压在桌上

branches.en: A statement made firm by the speaker.
branches.cn: 说话人把陈述钉稳。

branches.en: The same firmness given by evidence or authority.
branches.cn: 由证据或权威赋予的同一种稳固。

branches.en: A principle held firm against doubt.
branches.cn: 在怀疑面前握稳的原则。

branches.en: A ruling made firm again by a higher court.
branches.cn: 由上级法院重新钉稳的判决。

branches.en: Confirmation in words and confirmation in law.
branches.cn: 言辞上的确认与法律上的确认。

intro.en: Affirm is a clean Latin prefix-plus-adjective construction, and its family is equally transparent.
intro.cn: affirm 是清晰的拉丁语「前缀加形容词」构词，它的词族同样透明。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus firmus made affirmare; English kept both the verb and the adjective firm.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 firmus 构成 affirmare；英语既保留了动词，也保留了形容词 firm。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

items.exampleCN: 正在肯定的；正在确认的

latinEntries.example: Firmus is the root of affirm.
latinEntries.exampleCN: firmus 是 affirm 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Affirmare passed into Old French and English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affirmare 经由古法语进入英语。

definition_zh: （名词）词缀；附加物；（动词）附上；粘贴；盖（印）
definition_en: a letter or letters added to a word to form a new word; to attach or fasten something to a surface
core_image: 一枚被贴上去的小标签：附在词根或物体上
scene: 旧书摊的桌上放着一叠信封，摊主正把一枚邮票按在右上角。He affixed a stamp to the corner of the envelope.
sceneCN: 这里 affixed 是「贴上、粘上」（第 3 个义项：把某物固定到另一物表面）；句意为他把一枚邮票贴在信封的角上。画面中可辨识：旧书摊、信封、邮票。

derivatives.zh: 由 affix 加 -ation 构成，义为「词缀法；附加过程」
由 affix 加 -al 构成，义为「词缀的；与词缀有关的」

senses.title: A word element added to a root
senses.definition: a letter or group of letters added to the beginning or end of a word to change its meaning or form
senses.definitionCN: 加在词首或词尾、用以改变词义或词形的字母或字母组合
senses.example: The prefix un- is a common affix in English.
senses.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 是英语中常见的词缀。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the physical verb: a prefix or suffix is fastened onto a root just as a label is fastened onto a box.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了这个物理动词：前缀或后缀就像标签贴到盒子上一样，被固定在词根上。

senses.title: Something attached as an addition
senses.definition: a thing attached or added to something else, often as a minor addition
senses.definitionCN: 附加或添加到另一物上的东西，常指次要的添加物
senses.example: The contract had a short affix listing two extra duties.
senses.exampleCN: 合同后面附了一份简短的附加条款，列出两项额外义务。
senses.why: The noun keeps the literal sense: whatever has been fastened on becomes an affix.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了字面义：凡是被固定上去的东西，就成为一个 affix。

senses.title: To attach or fasten to a surface
senses.definition: to attach, fasten, or stick something onto a surface or object
senses.definitionCN: 把某物附着、固定或粘贴到某个表面或物体上
senses.example: He affixed a stamp to the corner of the envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一枚邮票贴在信封的角上。
senses.why: The Latin past participle meant fastened to, and the verb still means exactly that, with no metaphor needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语过去分词意为「固定于」，这个动词至今仍是这个意思，完全不需要比喻。

senses.title: To add a signature or seal
senses.definition: to add a signature, seal, or mark to a document in a formal way
senses.definitionCN: 在文件上正式加上签名、印章或标记
senses.example: Both parties affixed their seals to the agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 双方都在协议上盖了章。
senses.why: A seal is literally pressed onto paper, so this official sense is only the physical act made legal.
senses.whyCN: 印章确实是压在纸上的，所以这个正式义只是把物理动作放进了法律程序。

intro.en: Affix comes from a Latin verb meaning 'to fasten to', and its grammatical sense is a later borrowing of that physical image.
intro.cn: affix 来自拉丁语动词「固定到」，其语法义是后来从这个物理意象借来的。

items.en: Figere meant 'to fasten, fix, drive in', and it also gave English fix.
items.cn: figere 意为「固定、钉入」，它也给了英语 fix 这个词。

items.en: Affigere meant 'to fasten to, attach', built from ad- and figere.
items.cn: affigere 意为「固定到、附上」，由 ad- 与 figere 构成。

items.en: The past participle affixus meant 'fastened to' and became the English noun and adjective stem.
items.cn: 过去分词 affixus 意为「固定于」，成为英语名词与形容词的词干。

items.en: English used affix first for a thing fastened on, then adopted it for word elements in grammar.
items.cn: 英语先用 affix 指被固定上去的东西，后来在语法中用它指词缀。

items.en: Affixation became the standard term for the process of adding prefixes and suffixes.
items.cn: affixation 成为表示添加前缀与后缀这一过程的标准术语。

note.en: The first group gathers words from the same 'fasten' root; the second gathers word-formation and attachment terms.
note.cn: 第一组收同一「固定」词根的一族词；第二组收构词与附着类术语。

entries.definition: The process of adding an affix to a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「词缀法；附加过程」，由 affix 加 -ation 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to an affix or to affixes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「词缀的」，由 affix 加 -al 构成。

entries.definition: To repair something or fasten it in place.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修理；固定」，与 affix 同出拉丁语 figere「固定」。

entries.definition: An affix added to the beginning of a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「前缀」，是 affix 的一种，位于词首。

entries.definition: An affix added to the end of a word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后缀」，是 affix 的一种，位于词尾。

entries.definition: Something fastened or joined to another thing.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附件；附着物」，与义项二相近，但更强调连接关系。

normalIntro.en: Affix is best held by the word fix: an affix is something fixed onto something else.
normalIntro.cn: affix 可以靠 fix 这个词来记：affix 就是被固定到别处的东西。

normal.en: Fix means fasten, and af- is the assimilated form of ad-, so affix is to fasten to.
normal.cn: fix 意为「固定」，af- 是 ad- 的同化形式，所以 affix 就是「固定到」。

normal.en: A prefix is an affix at the front and a suffix is an affix at the end.
normal.cn: prefix 是位于词首的 affix，suffix 是位于词尾的 affix。

normal.en: To affix a stamp is the everyday physical use that keeps the original image alive.
normal.cn: affix a stamp「贴邮票」是让原始意象保持鲜活的日常用法。

normal.en: Affixation names the process, and affixal describes anything about affixes.
normal.cn: affixation 指这个过程，affixal 描述与词缀有关的事物。

normal.en: The noun stress falls on the first syllable, while the verb is often unstressed differently.
normal.cn: 名词重音落在第一个音节，动词的读法常常不同。

abstract.en: Picture a small sticker pressed onto the corner of a page, easy to miss but impossible to remove without a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小贴纸压在书页角上，容易忽略，却一撕就会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Think of a word as a body and an affix as a piece of clothing put on at the edge.
abstract.cn: 把一个词想成身体，把词缀想成穿在边缘的一件衣服。

abstract.en: See the same hand that fixes a stamp also fixing meaning onto a root.
abstract.cn: 想象贴邮票的那只手，也在把意义固定到词根上。

examples.en: The affix -ness turns adjectives into nouns.
examples.cn: 词缀 -ness 把形容词变成名词。

examples.en: Please affix your signature to the bottom of the form.
examples.cn: 请在表格底部签上你的名字。

examples.en: The parcel had no return address on it.
examples.cn: 包裹上没有寄件人的地址。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿菲克斯」——阿（a）菲（fei）克（ke）斯（si），把东西固定上去，就像词缀贴在词根上。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 figere「固定」构成 affigere「固定到」，过去分词 affixus 成为英语的 affix；作动词时读「/əˈfɪks/」。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a physical act of fastening, then splits into the thing fastened on and the grammar term for letters fastened to a root.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初是物理上的「固定」动作，随后分成两条线：被固定上去的东西，以及语法中固定在词根上的字母。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small label pressed onto a surface
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚压在某物表面的小标签

branches.en: Letters fastened to a root to make a new word.
branches.cn: 固定在词根上以构成新词的字母。

branches.en: Any object fastened on as an addition.
branches.cn: 作为附加物固定上去的任何物件。

branches.en: The physical act of sticking something on.
branches.cn: 把某物贴上去的物理动作。

branches.en: A seal or signature pressed onto a document.
branches.cn: 压在文件上的印章或签名。

branches.en: Everyday sticking and formal sealing as one action.
branches.cn: 日常粘贴与正式盖章是同一个动作。

intro.en: Affix is a Latin verb form that became both a noun and a verb in English, with a small but clear family.
intro.cn: affix 是拉丁语动词形式，在英语中同时成为名词与动词，词族不大却清楚。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus figere produced affigere, whose participle affixus English borrowed directly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 figere 构成 affigere，英语直接借用了它的分词形式 affixus。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

items.meaning: more than one, or he does

latinEntries.example: Figere also gave English fix.
latinEntries.exampleCN: figere 也给了英语 fix。

latinEntries.example: Affixus became the English affix.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affixus 成为英语的 affix。

definition_zh: 折磨；使痛苦；使苦恼；（疾病）侵袭
definition_en: to cause pain, suffering, or distress to someone, often repeatedly or over a long period
core_image: 一记反复落下的打击，让人长期受苦
scene: 雨季里，村庄的道路被洪水冲断，病人要走很远才能找到医生。Chronic pain afflicted him for most of his adult life.
sceneCN: 这里 afflicted 是「折磨、使受苦」（第 1 个义项：给身体或精神带来持续痛苦）；句意为慢性疼痛折磨了他成年后的大部分岁月。画面中可辨识：被冲断的道路、拄杖的病人、远处的诊所。

derivatives.zh: 由 afflict 加 -ion 构成，义为「痛苦；苦难；折磨人的病痛」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「受折磨的；患病的」
由 afflict 加 -ive 构成，义为「令人痛苦的；造成苦难的」

senses.title: To cause pain or suffering
senses.definition: to cause pain or suffering to a person or group, especially over time
senses.definitionCN: 给人或群体带来痛苦或苦难，尤指持续性的
senses.example: Chronic pain afflicted him for most of his adult life.
senses.exampleCN: 慢性疼痛折磨了他成年后的大部分岁月。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to strike something down, so suffering is pictured as blow after blow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「击倒」，所以苦难被想象成一记接一记的打击。

senses.title: Of a disease: to attack
senses.definition: of an illness or condition, to attack a person or a part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或病症侵袭某人或身体某部位
senses.example: A rare skin disease afflicted the workers in the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 一种罕见的皮肤病侵袭了那座旧工厂里的工人。
senses.why: A disease arrives like a series of blows the body cannot ward off, which is why the verb fits illness so well.
senses.whyCN: 疾病到来就像身体挡不住的一连串打击，所以这个动词特别适合描述疾病。

senses.title: To bring hardship to a place or group
senses.definition: to cause hardship, disaster, or serious difficulty for a place or community
senses.definitionCN: 给某地或某群体带来困苦、灾难或严重困难
senses.example: Drought and failed harvests afflicted the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱和歉收让整个地区陷入苦难。
senses.why: The blows can fall on a whole community, not only on one body, so the word extends to shared hardship.
senses.whyCN: 打击可以落在整个社区而不只是一个人身上，于是这个词扩展到共同的苦难。

senses.title: To trouble the mind
senses.definition: to distress or trouble someone mentally, especially with worry or doubt
senses.definitionCN: 在精神上使某人痛苦或困扰，尤指忧虑与疑虑
senses.example: Doubts about the decision afflicted her for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 对这个决定的疑虑折磨了她好几个星期。
senses.why: What strikes the body can also strike the mind, and this sense names the inward version of the same pain.
senses.whyCN: 打击身体的东西也能打击心灵，这个义项指的是同一种痛苦转向内心的形态。

intro.en: Afflict comes from Latin verbs of striking, and its core image is a blow that keeps falling.
intro.cn: afflict 来自拉丁语表示「打击」的动词，核心意象是一记不断落下的打击。

items.en: Fligere meant 'to strike, dash', and it also lies behind conflict.
items.cn: fligere 意为「打击、猛撞」，它也是 conflict 的词源成分。

items.en: Affligere meant 'to dash down, strike against, ruin', built with ad- and fligere.
items.cn: affligere 意为「击倒、撞击、毁坏」，由 ad- 与 fligere 构成。

items.en: The frequentative afflictare meant 'to keep striking, harass, torment'.
items.cn: 反复动词 afflictare 意为「不断打击、骚扰、折磨」。

items.en: English borrowed the Latin participle afflictus, partly through French, as the verb afflict.
items.cn: 英语经由法语借入拉丁语分词 afflictus，形成动词 afflict。

items.en: The medical and mental senses settled beside the older sense of external hardship.
items.cn: 医学义与精神义在较早的「外在困苦」义旁稳定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same 'strike' root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of causing pain and hardship.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「打击」词根的一族词；近义组收造成痛苦与困苦的动词。

entries.definition: A condition of pain, suffering, or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「痛苦；苦难；病痛」，由 afflict 加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: Suffering from pain, illness, or hardship.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受折磨的；患病的」，是 afflict 的过去分词。

entries.definition: A serious disagreement or a fight between opposing forces.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冲突；争斗」，与 afflict 同出拉丁语 fligere「打击」，但前缀不同。

entries.definition: To cause someone severe and lasting suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「折磨」，痛苦程度比 afflict 更重，常带持续性。

entries.definition: To cause continual trouble or distress to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不断困扰；使遭灾」，强调反复与恼人。

entries.definition: To make someone feel very worried, unhappy, or uncomfortable.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使痛苦；使忧虑」，侧重情绪上的难受。

normalIntro.en: Afflict is held by the image of a strike and by its large family of nouns and adjectives.
normalIntro.cn: afflict 可以靠「打击」这个意象，以及它成串的名词与形容词来记。

normal.en: Fligere means strike, so afflict is to strike someone down with pain.
normal.cn: fligere 意为「打击」，所以 afflict 就是用痛苦把人击倒。

normal.en: Affliction is the pain itself, and afflicted describes the person who carries it.
normal.cn: affliction 是痛苦本身，afflicted 描述承受痛苦的人。

normal.en: Be afflicted with is the passive phrase used for illness and hardship.
normal.cn: be afflicted with 是用于疾病与困苦的被动搭配。

normal.en: Conflict shares the same strike root but adds a different prefix meaning together.
normal.cn: conflict 共享同一「打击」词根，只是前缀表示「共同」。

normal.en: Afflictive is the adjective for whatever causes the suffering.
normal.cn: afflictive 是形容造成痛苦之物的形容词。

abstract.en: Picture a hammer that keeps falling on the same spot, never quite stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象一把锤子反复落在同一个地方，始终停不下来。

abstract.en: Think of a weight carried on the shoulders for years, invisible to others.
abstract.cn: 想象一副在肩上压了多年的重担，别人却看不见。

abstract.en: See the word as rain that will not stop: at first it is weather, then it becomes hardship.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一场停不下来的雨：起初只是天气，后来就成了苦难。

examples.en: The region has been afflicted by drought for three years.
examples.cn: 这个地区已经遭受旱灾三年。

examples.en: She was afflicted with a severe headache before the exam.
examples.cn: 考试前她饱受剧烈头痛的折磨。

examples.en: The village rebuilt its bridge the following spring.
examples.cn: 村庄在第二年春天重建了桥梁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗利克特」——阿（a）弗（fu）利（li）克（ke）特（te），一记记打击不断落在身上。

root: 拉丁语 fligere「打击」加前缀 ad- 构成 affligere「击倒」，其反复动词 afflictare 意为「不断折磨」，英语借入分词形式 afflictus。

sensesIntro.en: One image of repeated blows expands outward: physical pain, disease, communal hardship, and finally mental trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: 「反复打击」这一意象向外扩展：身体疼痛、疾病、群体困苦，最后是精神上的困扰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: blow after blow falling on the same spot
core.cn: 核心意象：一记接一记落在同一处的打击

branches.en: Pain pictured as repeated blows.
branches.cn: 把痛苦想象成反复的打击。

branches.en: A disease delivering those blows.
branches.cn: 疾病送来这些打击。

branches.en: The blows landing on a whole community.
branches.cn: 打击落在整个社区身上。

branches.en: The same blows turned inward on the mind.
branches.cn: 同样的打击转向内心。

branches.en: Pain for one body and hardship for a group.
branches.cn: 一个人的疼痛与一群人的困苦。

intro.en: Afflict is built from a prefix and a Latin root of striking, and its family is mostly suffixes added to the same stem.
intro.cn: afflict 由前缀与表示「打击」的拉丁词根构成，其词族主要是同一词干加后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus fligere gave affligere, and the participle afflictus gave English its stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 fligere 构成 affligere，分词 afflictus 为英语提供了词干。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Fligere is the root of afflict and conflict.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fligere 是 afflict 与 conflict 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Afflictare strengthened the sense of repeated pain.
latinEntries.exampleCN: afflictare 强化了反复痛苦的含义。

definition_zh: 富裕的；富足的；（地区）高档的；丰富的
definition_en: having a lot of money and a high standard of living; plentiful or abundant
core_image: 水源源不断流进来的样子：钱与资源充盈
scene: 河岸边的山坡上，新盖的房子一栋接一栋，花园里种着整齐的树。The affluent suburb has large houses, private schools, and quiet streets.
sceneCN: 这里 affluent 是「富裕的」（第 1 个义项：拥有大量钱财、生活水准高）；句意为这个富裕的郊区有大房子、私立学校和安静的街道。画面中可辨识：山坡住宅、花园、安静的街道。

derivatives.zh: 由 affluent 去掉词尾加 -ence 构成，义为「富裕；丰裕」
由 affluent 加 -ly 构成，义为「富裕地；丰足地」
由 affluent 与 influenza 缩合而成，指过度追求物质带来的「富裕病」，属非正式用词

senses.title: Having plenty of money
senses.definition: having a great deal of money and a high standard of living
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量钱财、生活水准很高
senses.example: The affluent couple donated a large sum to the library.
senses.exampleCN: 这对富裕的夫妇向图书馆捐了一大笔钱。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to flow toward, and the image is resources flowing in without stopping.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词意为「流向」，意象是资源不停地流进来。

senses.title: Of a place: wealthy and comfortable
senses.definition: of an area or neighbourhood, inhabited by wealthy people and offering expensive services
senses.definitionCN: 指地区或街区住着富裕人群、提供昂贵服务
senses.example: They moved to an affluent suburb with a private school nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 他们搬到了一个附近有私立学校的富裕郊区。
senses.why: Wealth spreads across a map: when many rich households cluster, the place itself is called affluent.
senses.whyCN: 财富会铺到地图上：当许多富裕家庭聚集，这个地方本身就被称为 affluent。

senses.title: Existing in abundance
senses.definition: present in large quantities; plentiful, used especially in formal writing
senses.definitionCN: 大量存在的、充裕的，尤用于正式书面语
senses.example: The valley had affluent supplies of water and timber.
senses.exampleCN: 这个山谷拥有充裕的水源和木材。
senses.why: The original sense was simply flowing plentifully, before money narrowed the word in everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 最初的意思只是「大量流动」，在日常生活里才被钱的意义收窄。

senses.title: Flowing freely, in older use
senses.definition: flowing freely or in abundance, an older and now rare sense
senses.definitionCN: 自由地或大量地流动，这一义项较古老，现今罕用
senses.example: The old poem describes an affluent stream that never dries.
senses.exampleCN: 那首古老的诗描写一条永不干涸的丰沛溪流。
senses.why: Before it named money, the word described water moving in quantity; that literal sense survives mainly in old texts.
senses.whyCN: 在指钱之前，这个词描述的是大量流动的水；这一字面义主要残留在旧文本里。

intro.en: Affluent is built on a Latin verb for flowing, and wealth was originally pictured as a flow of resources.
intro.cn: affluent 建立在拉丁语表示「流动」的动词上，财富最初被想象成资源的流动。

items.en: Fluere meant 'to flow', and it also gave English fluent and fluid.
items.cn: fluere 意为「流动」，它也给了英语 fluent 与 fluid。

items.en: Affluere meant 'to flow to, to flow in abundance', built with ad- and fluere.
items.cn: affluere 意为「流向、大量涌入」，由 ad- 与 fluere 构成。

items.en: Affluentia named abundance and the flow of wealth or supplies.
items.cn: affluentia 指丰裕，以及财富或物资的流入。

items.en: English first used affluent for flowing abundantly, then for people with abundant means.
items.cn: 英语最初用 affluent 表示「大量流动」，后来才指拥有丰裕资财的人。

items.en: The wealth sense became dominant, while the literal water sense retreated to older texts.
items.cn: 财富义成为主流，字面的水流义退回到旧文本中。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same 'flow' root; the near-meaning group gathers words for wealth and comfort.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「流动」词根的一族词；近义组收表示财富与富足生活的词。

entries.definition: A state of having a lot of money and material goods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「富裕；丰裕」，是 affluent 的名词形式。

entries.definition: Able to speak or write a language easily and smoothly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「流利的」，与 affluent 同出拉丁语 fluere「流动」，但前缀不同。

entries.definition: The place where two rivers flow together, or a coming together of things.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「汇流处；汇集」，同样来自 fluere「流动」。

entries.definition: Having a large amount of money, property, or valuable things.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富有的」，与 affluent 义项一几乎同义，更直白。

entries.definition: Successful and financially strong, especially of a person or region.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「繁荣的；兴旺的」，侧重发展与成功，而非单纯拥有钱财。

entries.definition: Having enough money to live comfortably.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽裕的；日子好过的」，程度比 affluent 温和。

entries.definition: Existing in large amounts, more than enough.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充足的；大量的」，对应义项三，但不含财富义。

normalIntro.en: Affluent is anchored by the root flu, which means flow, and by the picture of money flowing in.
normalIntro.cn: affluent 可以靠表示「流动」的词根 flu，以及钱不断流入的画面来记。

normal.en: Flu means flow, and affluere means to flow toward, so affluent is 'flowing in with resources'.
normal.cn: flu 意为「流动」，affluere 意为「流向」，所以 affluent 就是「资源源源流入」。

normal.en: Affluence is the noun for the state, and affluently is the adverb.
normal.cn: affluence 是表示状态的名词，affluently 是副词。

normal.en: An affluent suburb is a place where wealthy households cluster.
normal.cn: affluent suburb 是富裕家庭聚集的地方。

normal.en: Fluent and fluid share the same root, which keeps the flow image in view.
normal.cn: fluent 与 fluid 共享同一词根，让「流动」的意象始终可见。

normal.en: The phrase the affluent treats the adjective as a collective noun.
normal.cn: 「the affluent」这个说法把形容词当作集合名词使用。

abstract.en: Picture a river of coins running past a house and never running dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一条硬币组成的河从房前流过，永不干涸。

abstract.en: Think of a garden where the sprinkler is always on and the soil is always dark with water.
abstract.cn: 想象一座花园，喷头一直开着，土壤总是被水浸得发黑。

abstract.en: See wealth as a current rather than a pile: what matters is how much keeps arriving.
abstract.cn: 把财富看成水流而不是堆叠：重要的是有多少在不断到来。

examples.en: The affluent neighbourhood has its own marina and tennis club.
examples.cn: 这个富裕的街区有自己的游艇码头和网球俱乐部。

examples.en: Affluent families often spend more on tutoring than on holidays.
examples.cn: 富裕家庭花在辅导上的钱常常比花在度假上的更多。

examples.en: The river ran clear after the spring rains.
examples.cn: 春雨过后，河水清澈地流着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗伦特」——阿（a）弗（fu）伦（lun）特（te），钱像水一样不断流进来，日子就富裕了。

root: 拉丁语 ad-「向」加 fluere「流动」构成 affluere「流入、丰沛」，其名词 affluentia 指丰裕；英语先指「大量流动」，后专指富裕。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as water flowing in abundance, then narrows to money, then widens again to rich places and plentiful supplies.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指水大量流动，后收窄为钱财，再扩展为富裕地区与充裕物资。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: resources flowing in like a stream
core.cn: 核心意象：资源像溪流一样不断流入

branches.en: Money flowing into a household.
branches.cn: 钱财流入家庭。

branches.en: Wealth written across a whole district.
branches.cn: 财富铺展在整个街区。

branches.en: Supplies present in large quantity.
branches.cn: 大量存在的物资。

branches.en: The old literal sense of water flowing freely.
branches.cn: 水流自由流动的古老字面义。

branches.en: Abundance in money and abundance in goods.
branches.cn: 钱财的丰裕与物资的丰裕。

intro.en: Affluent is a prefix plus the Latin root for flow, with a family that spreads across several everyday words.
intro.cn: affluent 是前缀加拉丁语「流动」词根，其词族分布在好几个日常词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin ad- plus fluere made affluere, and fluentia supplied the noun affluence.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ad- 加 fluere 构成 affluere，fluentia 则提供了名词 affluence。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 f 前的同化形式

latinEntries.example: Fluere is the root of affluent and fluent.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fluere 是 affluent 与 fluent 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Affluentia gave English affluence.
latinEntries.exampleCN: affluentia 给了英语 affluence。

definition_zh: 买得起；负担得起；有条件（做）；提供；给予
definition_en: to have enough money or resources for something; to be able to do something without serious risk; to provide or give something
core_image: 口袋里有足够的余量，能把这件事承担下来
scene: 月底的餐桌上，父母对着账单算了很久，最后还是决定让孩子去参加那次远行。They could not afford the trip to the coast that summer.
sceneCN: 这里 afford 是「负担得起」（第 1 个义项：有钱支付某事物的费用）；句意为那年夏天他们负担不起去海边的旅行。画面中可辨识：餐桌、账单、旅行宣传单。

pos.zh: 买得起；负担得起；提供；给予

derivatives.zh: 由 afford 加 -able 构成，义为「负担得起的；价格合理的」
由 affordable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可负担性；价格可承受程度」

senses.title: To have enough money for something
senses.definition: to have enough money to pay for something without ruinous difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 有足够的钱支付某事物，而不至于造成严重困难
senses.example: They could not afford the trip to the coast that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那年夏天他们负担不起去海边的旅行。
senses.why: The old English word meant to further or accomplish, and the modern sense asks whether your means can carry the plan through.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语词意为「推进、完成」，现代义则是在问你的财力能否把这件计划办成。

senses.title: To be in a position to do something
senses.definition: to be able to do something without serious risk or loss, often used with time or energy
senses.definitionCN: 能够做某事而不冒严重风险或损失，常与时间、精力连用
senses.example: We cannot afford to waste another week.
senses.exampleCN: 我们耗不起再浪费一个星期。
senses.why: Means are not only money: time and strength are also budgets, and the verb asks whether you can spare them.
senses.whyCN: 可支配的不只是钱：时间和精力也是预算，这个动词在问你是否抽得出。

senses.title: To provide or give
senses.definition: to provide or give something such as an opportunity, protection, or pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 提供机会、保护或乐趣等事物
senses.example: The quiet garden afforded him a place to think.
senses.exampleCN: 这座安静的花园给了他一个思考的地方。
senses.why: If your means can carry a plan, they can also yield something for others, so the verb extends to giving.
senses.whyCN: 如果你的财力能托起一项计划，它也能为别人产出些什么，于是这个动词扩展到「给予」。

senses.title: To bear the risk or consequence
senses.definition: to be able to accept the cost, risk, or consequence of an action
senses.definitionCN: 能够承受某项行动带来的代价、风险或后果
senses.example: The company cannot afford another failed launch.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司承受不起又一次失败的发布。
senses.why: This is the money sense grown abstract: what you can carry includes bad outcomes, not only bills.
senses.whyCN: 这是钱财义的抽象化：你能承担的东西也包括坏结果，而不只是账单。

intro.en: Afford is a native English word, not a Latin borrowing, and its early sense was to accomplish or further something.
intro.cn: afford 是英语本族词，不是拉丁语借词，早期意思是「完成、推进」某事。

items.en: Forth meant 'forward, onward', and it survives in English phrases such as bring forth.
items.cn: forth 意为「向前、往外」，还保留在 bring forth 等英语说法里。

items.en: Geforthian meant 'to further, promote, accomplish', built on the same forward idea.
items.cn: geforthian 意为「推进、促进、完成」，建立在同一个「向前」的概念上。

items.en: The verb weakened to aforthen, with senses of managing, supplying, and being able to meet a cost.
items.cn: 这个动词弱化为 aforthen，带有「设法办到、供给、付得起」等意思。

items.en: The modern spelling afford settled, and the sense 'have the means for' became central.
items.cn: 现代拼写 afford 固定下来，「有财力做某事」成为核心义。

items.en: Affordable and affordability grew into everyday words in housing, health care, and shopping.
items.cn: affordable 与 affordability 成为住房、医疗与购物语境中的日常词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own derivatives and a spelling neighbour; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of managing, providing, and bearing cost.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的派生词与一个拼写相近的词；近义组收支付、提供与承受代价类动词。

entries.definition: Cheap enough for most people to pay for.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「负担得起的」，由 afford 加 -able 构成。

entries.definition: The degree to which something can be paid for by ordinary people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可负担性」，指普通人能否支付得起。

entries.definition: A shallow place in a river where you can walk across.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「浅滩；可涉水而过之处」；只是拼写与 afford 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To succeed in doing something despite difficulty, often with limited means.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「设法做到」，与义项二相近，强调在困难中仍能办成。

entries.definition: To give someone something they need or want.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提供；供给」，对应义项三，但不含支付能力的意思。

entries.definition: To accept or endure a cost, burden, or responsibility.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「承担；承受」，与义项四相近，更强调忍受重量。

normalIntro.en: Afford is a native word tied to 'forward', and it is best held by the phrase can afford.
normalIntro.cn: afford 是与「向前」相关的本族词，最好借 can afford 这个说法来记。

normal.en: The old word meant to further a plan, so affording something is carrying the plan through.
normal.cn: 这个古词意为推进计划，所以 afford 某物就是把计划托着办下去。

normal.en: Can afford is the common frame, and it asks whether your means can bear the cost.
normal.cn: can afford 是常见框架，问的是你的财力能否承担这笔费用。

normal.en: Afford to do extends the idea from money to time, energy, and risk.
normal.cn: afford to do 把这个概念从钱扩展到时间、精力与风险。

normal.en: Affordable and affordability are its two most useful derivatives.
normal.cn: affordable 与 affordability 是它最有用的两个派生词。

normal.en: The a- in afford is not the Latin prefix ad-, which is a common trap.
normal.cn: afford 里的 a- 并不是拉丁前缀 ad-，这是常见的误解。

abstract.en: Picture a pocket with just enough slack to hold one more coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一个口袋只剩一点点余量，正好还能装下一枚硬币。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge that can carry one more truck but not two.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥还能承受一辆卡车，却承受不了两辆。

abstract.en: See time as a purse too: spending a week is spending money you cannot earn back.
abstract.cn: 把时间也看成一个钱包：花掉一周，就是花掉挣不回来的钱。

examples.en: They could not afford the trip to the coast that summer.
examples.cn: 那年夏天他们负担不起去海边的旅行。

examples.en: The job afforded her a chance to work abroad.
examples.cn: 这份工作给了她一个到国外工作的机会。

examples.en: The bill arrived at the end of a long month.
examples.cn: 账单在漫长的一个月结束时到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿福德」——阿（a）福（fu）德（de），有福有德、手头宽裕，就负担得起。

root: 古英语 geforthian「推进、完成」来自 forth「向前」，中古英语弱化为 aforthen，后固定为 afford；开头的 a- 并非拉丁前缀 ad-。

sensesIntro.en: One budget image runs through the word: money, time, opportunity, and risk are all things you may or may not be able to carry.
sensesIntro.cn: 整条义项线贯穿着同一个「预算」意象：钱、时间、机会与风险，都是你可能承担得起也可能承担不起的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pocket with enough slack for one more thing
core.cn: 核心意象：一个还装得下一样东西的口袋

branches.en: Money enough to pay the price.
branches.cn: 足以支付价格的钱。

branches.en: Time or strength enough to attempt something.
branches.cn: 足以尝试某事的时间或精力。

branches.en: Means that yield something for others.
branches.cn: 能为他人产出些什么的财力。

branches.en: Capacity to carry a bad outcome.
branches.cn: 承受坏结果的能力。

branches.en: Paying a bill and paying for a mistake.
