branches.cn: 付账单与为错误付代价。

intro.en: Afford is native English, so its construction is mainly prefixes and suffixes added to a Germanic core rather than Latin roots.
intro.cn: afford 是英语本族词，其构词主要是日耳曼语核心加前后缀，而不是拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the -able in affordable, however, is a Latin suffix that reached English through French.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源；不过 affordable 里的 -able 是经法语进入英语的拉丁语后缀。

items.meaning: be able to do without ruin

definition_zh: 负担得起的；价格合理的；买得起的
definition_en: cheap enough that most people can pay for it; within someone's financial reach
core_image: 标价牌落在口袋能承受的范围之内
scene: 社区中心贴出通知，说新开的诊所提供价格低廉的检查服务。The clinic offers affordable care for families without insurance.
sceneCN: 这里 affordable 是「负担得起的、价格合理的」（第 1 个义项：费用低到普通人能支付）；句意为这家诊所为自己没有保险的家庭提供负担得起的医疗服务。画面中可辨识：社区通知、诊所门口、排队的人。

pos.zh: 负担得起的；价格合理的；买得起的

derivatives.zh: 由 affordable 加 -ity 构成，义为「可负担性；价格可承受程度」
由 affordable 加 -ly 构成，义为「以负担得起的方式；价格合理地」
由 un- 加 affordable 构成，义为「负担不起的；过于昂贵的」

senses.title: Cheap enough to be paid for
senses.definition: having a price low enough that ordinary people can pay it
senses.definitionCN: 价格低到普通人能够支付
senses.example: The clinic offers affordable care for families without insurance.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为自己没有保险的家庭提供负担得起的医疗服务。
senses.why: The suffix -able turns afford into a question of possibility: can your means carry this price?
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 把 afford 变成可能性的问题：你的财力能承担这个价格吗？

senses.title: Reasonable in cost relative to value
senses.definition: having a cost that is reasonable in relation to what you receive
senses.definitionCN: 相对所得而言成本合理的
senses.example: For a small car, it is an affordable option with low running costs.
senses.exampleCN: 作为小型车，它的价格合理，使用成本也低。
senses.why: Affordability is not only about being poor: a thing can be affordable because its price matches its value.
senses.whyCN: 可负担性不只关乎钱少：一件东西也可以因为价格与价值相称而显得划算。

senses.title: Of housing: within reach of ordinary incomes
senses.definition: of housing or services, priced so that people with ordinary incomes can obtain them
senses.definitionCN: 指住房或服务定价使普通收入者也能获得
senses.example: The city promised to build more affordable housing near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府承诺在车站附近建造更多经济适用住房。
senses.why: In policy language, affordable names a target, not a compliment: a price a normal salary can actually cover.
senses.whyCN: 在政策语言里，affordable 指一个目标而不是赞美：普通工资确实能覆盖的价格。

intro.en: Affordable is afford plus a Latin-derived suffix, and the word became prominent with housing and health care policy.
intro.cn: affordable 是 afford 加一个源自拉丁语的后缀，随着住房与医疗政策而变得常用。

items.en: The native verb behind afford meant to further or accomplish something.
items.cn: afford 背后的本族动词意为推进或完成某事。

items.en: The verb settled into the sense of having means for something.
items.cn: 这个动词逐渐固定为「有财力做某事」。

items.en: The suffix -abilis meant 'that can be done', and it reached English as -able through French.
items.cn: 后缀 -abilis 意为「可以被……的」，经法语以 -able 形式进入英语。

items.en: Affordable appears as a regular derivative meaning 'able to be afforded'.
items.cn: affordable 作为规则派生词出现，意为「负担得起的」。

items.en: Housing and health care debates made affordable a standard policy word in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 住房与医疗的讨论使 affordable 在二十世纪成为标准的政策用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's own family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives about low and reasonable prices.
note.cn: 形近组收本词自己的词族；近义组收表示低价与价格合理的形容词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to have enough money or means for something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「负担得起；提供」，是 affordable 的原词。

entries.definition: The extent to which something can be afforded by ordinary people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可负担性」，由 affordable 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: In a way that is within people's financial reach.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以负担得起的方式」，由 affordable 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: Costing little money, though sometimes suggesting poor quality.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「便宜的」，但常暗含质量不佳，不如 affordable 中性。

entries.definition: Not costing much money, used to avoid the negative tone of cheap.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不贵的」，比 cheap 更中性，常用于商品描述。

entries.definition: Fairly priced and not too expensive.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「价格公道的；合理的」，侧重价格与价值相称。

entries.definition: Good value because it saves money in use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「经济实惠的」，侧重长期使用省钱，而不只是标价低。

normalIntro.en: Affordable is simply afford plus -able, and the suffix turns an ability into a price judgement.
normalIntro.cn: affordable 就是 afford 加 -able，这个后缀把「能力」变成了对价格的判断。

normal.en: Break it as afford plus able: able to be afforded.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 afford 加 able：能够被负担得起。

normal.en: Affordability is the noun, and it is the word used in housing reports.
normal.cn: affordability 是名词，也是住房报告里常用的词。

normal.en: Affordably is the adverb, as in affordably priced.
normal.cn: affordably 是副词，如 affordably priced 表示「定价合理」。

normal.en: Unaffordable is its opposite, formed with un-.
normal.cn: unaffordable 是它的反义，由 un- 构成。

normal.en: In policy, affordable housing means housing a normal income can cover.
normal.cn: 在政策里，affordable housing 指普通收入能覆盖的住房。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag that fits inside a wallet without tearing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签正好能放进钱包，而不会把钱包撑破。

abstract.en: Think of a door handle placed low enough for a child to reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一个门把手装得足够低，孩子也够得到。

abstract.en: See affordability as a bridge between what something costs and what someone earns.
abstract.cn: 把可负担性看成标价与收入之间的一座桥。

examples.en: The city needs more affordable housing near public transport.
examples.cn: 这座城市需要在公共交通附近建造更多经济适用住房。

examples.en: They found an affordable option that still included breakfast.
examples.cn: 他们找到一个价格合理、还包含早餐的选择。

examples.en: The queue outside the clinic stretched around the block.
examples.cn: 诊所外的队伍一直排到了街角。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿福德伯」——阿（a）福（fu）德（de）伯（bo），有福的人手头宽裕，什么都买得起。

root: 由本族词 afford「负担得起」加后缀 -able「可以被……的」构成；-able 源自拉丁语 -abilis，经法语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective starts from a simple price test, then adds the idea of fair value, and finally becomes a housing-policy label.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个形容词从简单的价格测试出发，再加入「划算」的意思，最后成为住房政策的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price tag that fits inside a wallet
core.cn: 核心意象：一张能放进钱包的价签

branches.en: A price ordinary people can pay.
branches.cn: 普通人付得起的价格。

branches.en: A cost that matches what you receive.
branches.cn: 与所得相称的成本。

branches.en: A policy label for housing within normal incomes.
branches.cn: 指普通收入可以覆盖的住房政策标签。

branches.en: Cheap enough and fair enough at the same time.
branches.cn: 既足够便宜，又足够公道。

branches.en: Fair pricing turned into a public standard.
branches.cn: 公道定价转化为一项公共标准。

intro.en: Affordable is a native verb plus a borrowed suffix, a common pattern in modern English.
intro.cn: affordable 是本族动词加外来后缀，这是现代英语常见的模式。

latinIntro.en: The -able ending comes from Latin -abilis by way of French, while the stem afford is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾 -able 经法语来自拉丁语 -abilis，而词干 afford 属于日耳曼语。

items.meaning: in a way that can be

latinEntries.example: -abilis became -able in English.
latinEntries.exampleCN: -abilis 在英语中变成 -able。

definition_zh: 漂浮的；在海上；不负债的；在流传中
definition_en: floating on water; on a ship or at sea; free of debt and able to continue; in circulation
core_image: 水面托着一样东西：既没有沉下去，也没有靠岸
scene: 渔港的清晨，船身随着潮水轻轻起伏，缆绳在水面投下摇晃的影子。The old boat stayed afloat through the storm.
sceneCN: 这里 afloat 是「漂浮着的」（第 1 个义项：浮在水面上不沉）；句意为那条旧船在风暴中始终没有沉。画面中可辨识：渔港、起伏的船身、缆绳。

pos.zh: 漂浮的；不负债的；在流传中的
漂浮着；在海上；不欠债地

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（表语形容词）

derivatives.zh: afloat 去掉前缀后的词根动词，义为「漂浮；浮动」，与本词同族
由 float 加 -ing 构成，义为「漂浮的；流动的」，与本词同义场

senses.title: Floating on water
senses.definition: resting on the surface of water without sinking
senses.definitionCN: 停在水面上而没有下沉
senses.example: The old boat stayed afloat through the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 那条旧船在风暴中始终没有沉。
senses.why: The prefix a- means on, and float is the verb for resting on water, so afloat is literally 'on float'.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 a- 意为「在……上」，float 是「浮在水面」的动词，所以 afloat 字面就是「处于漂浮之中」。

senses.title: On a ship or at sea
senses.definition: on board a ship or out on the water, especially after leaving port
senses.definitionCN: 在船上或在水上，尤指离港之后
senses.example: The crew spent three months afloat before reaching land.
senses.exampleCN: 船员们在海上待了三个月才靠岸。
senses.why: Once a ship has left land, the whole life on board is literally afloat, so the word came to mean life at sea.
senses.whyCN: 船一旦离岸，船上的整个生活就确实处于漂浮状态，于是这个词也指海上生活。

senses.title: Free of debt and still operating
senses.titleCN: 不负债的；维持得下去的
senses.definition: of a business or person, able to pay debts and keep going
senses.definitionCN: 指企业或个人能偿付债务、继续运转
senses.example: Small grants kept the theatre afloat during the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 小额资助让这家剧院在冬天维持了下来。
senses.why: A business that does not sink is one that stays above its debts, so the water image moved to finance.
senses.whyCN: 没有沉下去的企业就是浮在债务之上的企业，于是水的意象搬到了财务上。

senses.title: In circulation or in the air
senses.definition: of rumours, ideas, or plans, being talked about or circulating
senses.definitionCN: 指谣言、想法或计划正在被谈论、传播
senses.example: There were rumours afloat that the factory would close.
senses.exampleCN: 当时有谣言在流传，说那家工厂要关闭。
senses.why: Words and stories can drift on the surface of a group just as a boat drifts on water.
senses.whyCN: 言辞与故事也能像船漂在水面一样，漂浮在一个群体的表面。

intro.en: Afloat is a native English phrase-word made of a prefix meaning 'on' and a verb for floating.
intro.cn: afloat 是英语本族的短语式合成词，由表示「在……上」的前缀与「漂浮」动词组成。

items.en: Flotian meant 'to float, to rest on water', and it is the direct source of float.
items.cn: flotian 意为「漂浮、浮在水面」，是 float 的直接来源。

items.en: The related noun flota meant 'ship, fleet', showing how early the water image spread.
items.cn: 相关名词 flota 意为「船、船队」，说明这个水的意象很早就扩展了。

items.en: The phrase on flote, literally 'on float', was reduced to the single word afloat.
items.cn: 短语 on flote 字面为「处于漂浮」，后来缩合成单词 afloat。

items.en: Afloat is recorded in the sense of floating on water and of being at sea.
items.cn: afloat 在十六至十七世纪有记录，义为「漂在水上」与「在海上」。

items.en: The financial sense 'out of debt, still operating' developed in modern business writing.
items.cn: 「不欠债、仍能运转」的财务义在现代商业写作中发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same float root; the near-meaning group gathers states of floating, drifting, and staying solvent.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 float 词根的一族词；近义组收漂浮、漂流与维持偿付的状态词。

entries.definition: To rest on the surface of water or to move gently through the air.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「漂浮；浮动」，是 afloat 的词根动词。

entries.definition: Resting on water or moving freely without being fixed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「漂浮的；流动的」，由 float 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: Wreckage or goods floating on the sea after a ship has been lost.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「漂浮的残骸；漂流物」，与 float 同源，多指海难后的漂浮物。

entries.definition: Able to float or to keep something afloat.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有浮力的；能漂浮的」，侧重浮力而非状态。

entries.definition: Floating without control or direction, often after breaking loose.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「漂泊的；随波逐流的」，强调失去控制与方向。

entries.definition: Having enough money to pay your debts.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有偿付能力的」，对应义项三的财务含义。

entries.definition: Spreading among people, as news or rumours do.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「流传中的」，对应义项四的传播含义。

normalIntro.en: Afloat is held by its simple structure: a- 'on' plus float, and by the business phrase stay afloat.
normalIntro.cn: afloat 可以靠它简单的结构来记：a- 表示「在……上」，加 float；再靠 stay afloat 这个说法固定。

normal.en: A- means on, so afloat is 'on float', resting on the water.
normal.cn: a- 意为「在……上」，所以 afloat 就是「处于漂浮」，停在水面上。

normal.en: Stay afloat is the phrase for a boat that does not sink and a business that does not fail.
normal.cn: stay afloat 既指船不沉，也指企业不倒。

normal.en: Float is the verb, floating is the adjective, and afloat is the state.
normal.cn: float 是动词，floating 是形容词，afloat 是状态。

normal.en: Set afloat can mean launch a ship or spread a rumour.
normal.cn: set afloat 既可指让船下水，也可指让谣言传开。

normal.en: The word has no comparative form because it describes a state, not a degree.
normal.cn: 这个词没有比较级，因为它描述的是状态而不是程度。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf holding its place on a moving river, neither sinking nor reaching the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子在流动的河面上保持位置，既不下沉，也不靠岸。

abstract.en: Think of a shop that pays its bills each month and never quite closes.
abstract.cn: 想象一家每月付清账单、始终没有关门的店铺。

abstract.en: See a rumour as a bottle bobbing on the surface of a crowd.
abstract.cn: 把谣言看成一个在人海表面上下浮动的瓶子。

examples.en: The life jacket kept him afloat until the boat arrived.
examples.cn: 救生衣让他在水面上坚持到船来。

examples.en: The magazine stayed afloat thanks to a few loyal readers.
examples.cn: 多亏几位忠实读者，这本杂志才维持了下来。

examples.en: The harbour lights came on one by one.
examples.cn: 港口的灯一盏接一盏亮了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗洛特」——阿（a）弗（fu）洛（luo）特（te），漂在水面上，不沉也不靠岸。

root: 由 a-「在……上」加 float「漂浮」构成；float 来自古英语 flotian「漂浮」，与 flota「船、船队」同族。

sensesIntro.en: One water state spreads into four: floating, being at sea, staying above debt, and drifting through a crowd as rumour.
sensesIntro.cn: 一种水面状态扩展成四种：漂浮、在海上、浮在债务之上，以及像谣言一样在人堆里漂。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something held up by water, neither sinking nor landing
core.cn: 核心意象：被水托着的东西，既不下沉也不靠岸

branches.en: The literal state of resting on water.
branches.cn: 停在水面上的字面状态。

branches.en: Life lived on a ship or at sea.
branches.cn: 在船上或海上度过的生活。

branches.en: A business kept above its debts.
branches.cn: 浮在债务之上、仍能运转的企业。

branches.en: Words drifting through a group.
branches.cn: 在人堆里漂流的言辞。

branches.en: Staying on the surface at sea and in finance.
branches.cn: 在海上与在财务上都保持在水面之上。

intro.en: Afloat is a prefix plus a native verb, and its family is mostly forms and derivatives of float.
intro.cn: afloat 是前缀加本族动词，其词族主要是 float 的各种形式与派生词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source in this word; the elements are Germanic and the prefix a- is a reduced form of on.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源；各成分属于日耳曼语，前缀 a- 是 on 的弱化形式。

definition_zh: 害怕的；担心的；不敢的；恐怕（礼貌用语）
definition_en: feeling fear or worry about something; unwilling to do something because of fear; used politely to apologize or give bad news
core_image: 心里往后缩的一步，面对可能到来的危险
scene: 深夜的走廊里，孩子听见楼梯间的响动，抓紧了母亲的衣角。The child was afraid of the dark staircase.
sceneCN: 这里 afraid 是「害怕的」（第 1 个义项：对某事物感到恐惧）；句意为孩子害怕那段漆黑的楼梯。画面中可辨识：深夜走廊、楼梯间、抓住衣角的孩子。

pos.zh: 害怕的；担心的；不敢的；（礼貌）恐怕

forms.label: 无比较级与最高级（表语形容词）

derivatives.zh: 由 un- 加 afraid 构成，义为「不怕的；无所畏惧的」
afraid 的古体变体，义同「害怕的」，多见于早期英语文本

senses.title: Feeling fear of something
senses.definition: feeling fear because of a person, thing, or situation
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人、某物或某种情况而感到恐惧
senses.example: The child was afraid of the dark staircase.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子害怕那段漆黑的楼梯。
senses.why: The word began as a participle meaning 'frightened', so the feeling is something done to you before it is something you do.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初是意为「被吓到」的分词，所以这种感受先是被施加于你，而不是你主动做出的。

senses.title: Worried about someone or something
senses.definition: worried that something bad may happen to a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 担心某人或某物可能遭遇不好的事
senses.example: She was afraid for her son, who had not called.
senses.exampleCN: 她为没有打电话来的儿子担心。
senses.why: Fear can point forward as worry: the danger is not here yet, but the mind already reaches toward it.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧可以向前延伸为担忧：危险还没到，心却已经伸向它了。

senses.title: Unwilling to act because of fear
senses.definition: unwilling to do something because of fear or doubt
senses.definitionCN: 因为害怕或疑虑而不愿做某事
senses.example: He was afraid to ask for help.
senses.exampleCN: 他不敢开口求助。
senses.why: When fear stands in front of an action, it becomes a refusal, and afraid to do names that barrier.
senses.whyCN: 当恐惧挡在动作前面，它就成了一种拒绝，afraid to do 指的就是这道障碍。

senses.title: Polite regret: I'm afraid
senses.definition: used politely to introduce an apology, a refusal, or unpleasant news
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地引出歉意、拒绝或坏消息
senses.example: I'm afraid the last train has already left.
senses.exampleCN: 恐怕末班车已经开走了。
senses.why: The fear sense softened into social caution: the speaker braces for the listener's disappointment.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧义软化为社交上的谨慎：说话者为听者的失望先做一点心理准备。

intro.en: Afraid began as a participle of a verb meaning 'to frighten', not as a word for fear itself.
intro.cn: afraid 起初是动词「使惊恐」的分词，而不是表示恐惧本身的词。

items.en: The prefix ex- 'out' combined with a Germanic word for peace in Vulgar Latin.
items.cn: 前缀 ex-「出」在俗拉丁语中与一个表示「和平」的日耳曼词结合。

items.en: Exfridare meant 'to disturb the peace, to frighten', literally to put someone out of peace.
items.cn: exfridare 意为「扰乱安宁、使惊恐」，字面是「把人从和平中赶出去」。

items.en: Old French esfreer meant 'to frighten, to alarm' and passed into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 esfreer 意为「使惊恐、使惊慌」，传入中古英语。

items.en: The verb affraien meant 'to frighten', and its participle became the adjective afraid.
items.cn: 动词 affraien 意为「使惊恐」，其分词演变为形容词 afraid。

items.en: Afraid settled as a predicate adjective and later took on the polite sense of I'm afraid.
items.cn: afraid 固定为表语形容词，后来又发展出 I'm afraid 的礼貌用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same frighten family; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for fear and worry.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「使惊恐」词族；近义组收表示恐惧与忧虑的形容词。

entries.definition: A public fight or disturbance that frightens people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「斗殴；扰乱治安」，与 afraid 同出古法语「使惊恐」的动词。

entries.definition: An archaic variant of afraid, meaning frightened.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，afraid 的古体变体，义为「害怕的」，多见于早期文本。

entries.definition: Not frightened; willing to face danger.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不怕的；无畏的」，由 un- 加 afraid 构成。

entries.definition: Feeling fear, especially suddenly.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「受惊的；害怕的」，强调突然被吓到。

entries.definition: Feeling fear, used especially in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「害怕的」，口语色彩强，常与 of 连用。

entries.definition: Feeling fear, or causing fear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「害怕的」或「可怕的」，比 afraid 更书面。

entries.definition: Worried about something that may happen.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「焦虑的；担心的」，对应义项二，但更强调持续不安。

normalIntro.en: Afraid is best remembered as the 'frightened' participle, with the polite phrase I'm afraid as its everyday anchor.
normalIntro.cn: afraid 最好记成「被吓到」的分词，再用 I'm afraid 这个日常说法固定它。

normal.en: The old verb meant to frighten, so afraid is the state of having been frightened.
normal.cn: 古动词意为「使惊恐」，所以 afraid 就是「被吓到」的状态。

normal.en: Be afraid of names the danger, and be afraid to do names the barrier to action.
normal.cn: be afraid of 引出危险对象，be afraid to do 引出行动的障碍。

normal.en: I'm afraid is not about fear at all; it is a polite way to soften bad news.
normal.cn: I'm afraid 与恐惧无关，它是让坏消息变柔和的礼貌说法。

normal.en: Unafraid simply adds un- and reverses the feeling.
normal.cn: unafraid 只是加了 un-，把这种感觉反过来。

normal.en: Affray shares the same frighten source but became a noun for a public disturbance.
normal.cn: affray 共享同一「使惊恐」来源，却变成了表示公共骚乱的名词。

abstract.en: Picture a child stepping back from a dark doorway without knowing why.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子从漆黑的门口后退一步，却说不出原因。

abstract.en: Think of fear as a hand on your shoulder pulling you away from the edge.
abstract.cn: 把恐惧想成一只搭在你肩上、把你从边缘拉回的手。

abstract.en: See the polite I'm afraid as a small bow before delivering a disappointment.
abstract.cn: 把礼貌的 I'm afraid 看成送出失望之前的一个小小鞠躬。

examples.en: The child was afraid of the dark staircase.
examples.cn: 孩子害怕那段漆黑的楼梯。

examples.en: I'm afraid we cannot change the booking now.
examples.cn: 恐怕我们现在无法更改预订了。

examples.en: The corridor light flickered twice and went out.
examples.cn: 走廊的灯闪了两下就灭了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿弗雷德」——阿（a）弗（fu）雷（lei）德（de），心里一害怕，脚步就往后退。

root: 俗拉丁语 exfridare「扰乱安宁、使惊恐」经古法语 esfreer 进入中古英语动词 affraien，其分词演变为表语形容词 afraid。

sensesIntro.en: From being frightened, the word spreads to worry, to unwillingness, and finally to a polite formula for bad news.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「被吓到」出发，这个词扩展到担忧、到不敢行动，最后变成引出坏消息的礼貌套语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a step taken backward from danger
core.cn: 核心意象：面对危险时往后缩的一步

branches.en: Fear with a clear object in front of it.
branches.cn: 面对明确对象时的恐惧。

branches.en: Fear stretched forward into worry.
branches.cn: 恐惧向前延伸为担忧。

branches.en: Fear turned into a refusal to act.
branches.cn: 恐惧转化为拒绝行动。

branches.en: Fear softened into social politeness.
branches.cn: 恐惧软化为社交礼貌。

branches.en: The feeling and the barrier it creates.
branches.cn: 这种感受以及它造成的障碍。

intro.en: Afraid is a fossilized participle, so its building blocks are best seen through related words rather than a clean prefix-plus-root split.
intro.cn: afraid 是凝固的分词，所以它的构词最好通过相关词来看，而不是干净地拆成前缀加词根。

latinIntro.en: The word came through Vulgar Latin and Old French, and its Latin pieces are ex- and a Germanic word for peace.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词经由俗拉丁语与古法语而来，其拉丁成分是 ex- 与一个表示「和平」的日耳曼词。

latinEntries.example: Exfridare became esfreer in Old French.
latinEntries.exampleCN: exfridare 在古法语中变成 esfreer。

latinEntries.example: Esfreer entered Middle English as affraien.
latinEntries.exampleCN: esfreer 作为 affraien 进入中古英语。

definition_zh: 在……之后；在……后面；追赶；仿照；（副词）以后
definition_en: following in time or place; later than; in pursuit of; in imitation of; as an adverb, later
core_image: 跟在后面的一步：时间或位置上的「在后」
scene: 散场后的剧院门口，人群慢慢散去，清洁工推着车走进空荡的大厅。We went for a walk after the play.
sceneCN: 这里 after 是「在……之后」（第 1 个义项：时间上晚于某事）；句意为演出结束后我们去散了步。画面中可辨识：剧院门口、散去的人群、清洁车。

pos.zh: 在……之后；在……后面；追赶；仿照

derivatives.zh: 由 after 加复数词尾构成，英式口语指「餐后甜点」
由 after 加 -wards 构成，义为「之后；后来」
复合词，由 after 与 glow 组成，义为「余晖；事后残留的愉悦」

senses.title: Later than an event
senses.definition: later in time than an event or period
senses.definitionCN: 在某个事件或时期之后的时间里
senses.example: We went for a walk after the play.
senses.exampleCN: 演出结束后我们去散了步。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply 'behind' in time, and English has kept it as the most common use.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是时间上的「在后面」，英语把它保留为最常见的用法。

senses.title: Behind in place or order
senses.definition: behind someone or something in place, rank, or order
senses.definitionCN: 在地点、等级或顺序上位于某人某物之后
senses.example: The letter A comes after the letter Z in the old index.
senses.exampleCN: 在那本旧索引里，字母 A 排在字母 Z 后面。
senses.why: The spatial sense is the twin of the temporal one: what follows is literally or figuratively behind.
senses.whyCN: 空间义与时间义是一对双生：跟在后面的东西，字面上或比喻上都处于后方。

senses.title: In pursuit of
senses.definition: following someone in order to catch them, or trying to obtain something
senses.definitionCN: 为了抓住某人而跟随，或力图获得某物
senses.example: The dog ran after the ball and brought it back.
senses.exampleCN: 狗追着球跑，把它叼了回来。
senses.why: To be after something is to place yourself behind it and keep moving, which is the physical shape of pursuit.
senses.whyCN: be after 某物，就是把自己放在它后面并持续移动，这正是追逐的物理形状。

senses.title: In imitation of
senses.definition: in the style of, or named in honour of someone
senses.definitionCN: 以某人的风格为准，或以某人的名字命名
senses.example: The street was named after a local doctor.
senses.exampleCN: 这条街以一位本地医生的名字命名。
senses.why: To follow someone in name or style is to come after them as a copy follows its model.
senses.whyCN: 在名字或风格上追随某人，就像复制品跟随原物一样，排在它之后。

senses.title: Later, as an adverb
senses.definition: at a later time, used without a following noun
senses.definitionCN: 在较晚的时间，后面不接名词
senses.example: She arrived soon after and found the door open.
senses.exampleCN: 她不久后赶到，发现门开着。
senses.why: The preposition shed its object and stood alone, becoming the adverb that simply means 'later'.
senses.whyCN: 介词丢掉了宾语独自站立，就成了只表示「后来」的副词。

intro.en: After is a native Germanic word whose original meaning was 'behind', and time grew out of space.
intro.cn: after 是日耳曼语本族词，原义为「在后面」，时间义是从空间义生长出来的。

items.en: The reconstructed form after meant 'behind, from behind', related to the idea of 'off, away'.
items.cn: 重构形式 after 意为「在后面、从后面」，与「离开、远离」的概念相关。

items.en: Old English æfter meant 'after, behind, later, in pursuit of', already covering space and time.
items.cn: 古英语 æfter 意为「在后、后面、后来、追赶」，已经同时覆盖空间与时间。

items.en: The spelling settled as after, and the word kept its prepositional and adverbial uses.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 after，这个词保留了介词与副词的用法。

items.en: The adverb afterwards, built with -wards, became the usual form for 'later on'.
items.cn: 由 -wards 构成的副词 afterwards 成为表示「后来」的常用形式。

items.en: Compounds such as afternoon and aftermath extended the word into fixed everyday nouns.
items.cn: afternoon 与 aftermath 等复合词把这个词扩展为固定的日常名词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words beginning with the same after element; the near-meaning group gathers words for later and behind.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以 after 起头的一族词；近义组收表示「后来」与「在后」的词。

entries.definition: At a later time; after an event has happened.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「之后；后来」，由 after 加 -wards 构成。

entries.definition: The consequences or after effects of a serious event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后果；余波」，是 after 与 math 构成的复合词。

entries.definition: The part of the day between noon and evening.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「下午」，是 after 与 noon 构成的复合词。

entries.definition: At a time after the present or after a stated time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来；较晚地」，对应义项五，最通用。

entries.definition: At the back of someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 介词或副词，义为「在……后面」，对应义项二的空间含义。

entries.definition: Coming after something in time or order.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词或介词，义为「接着的；在……之后」，比 after 正式。

entries.definition: The American form of afterwards, meaning later.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来」，是 afterwards 的美式拼写形式。

normalIntro.en: After is a spatial word that learned to tell time, and its compounds make the family easy to hold.
normalIntro.cn: after 是一个学会表达时间的空间词，它的复合词让这个词族容易掌握。

normal.en: The core image is behind, so after is first a place and then a time.
normal.cn: 核心意象是「在后面」，所以 after 先是位置，再是时间。

normal.en: After all is a fixed phrase meaning 'in the end', not a literal sequence.
normal.cn: after all 是表示「毕竟、终究」的固定说法，不是字面的先后顺序。

normal.en: Look after someone is to follow them with care, and the care sense grew from that.
normal.cn: look after 某人就是带着关心跟在他后面，照料的含义由此生长出来。

normal.en: Be after something means to pursue it, as if running behind it.
normal.cn: be after 某物就是追求它，像在它后面追赶。

normal.en: Afterwards, aftermath, and afternoon all begin with the same after element.
normal.cn: afterwards、aftermath 与 afternoon 都以同一个 after 成分起头。

abstract.en: Picture a second footprint always placed behind the first.
abstract.cn: 想象第二个脚印总是落在第一个脚印后面。

abstract.en: Think of a queue: everyone is after the person in front, and that is both place and time.
abstract.cn: 想象一条队伍：每个人都排在前面那人之后，这既是位置也是时间。

abstract.en: See the word as a shadow that follows an object wherever it goes.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成影子，物体走到哪里它就跟到哪里。

examples.en: We went for a walk after the play.
examples.cn: 演出结束后我们去散了步。

examples.en: The dog ran after the ball and brought it back.
examples.cn: 狗追着球跑，把它叼了回来。

examples.en: The theatre emptied slowly and the lights went out.
examples.cn: 剧院慢慢空了，灯也灭了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿夫特」——阿（a）夫（fu）特（te），跟在后面特别紧，时间和位置都在后。

root: 古英语 æfter「在后、后来、追赶」来自原始日耳曼语，原义为「在后面」；空间义后来延伸出时间义与追赶义。

sensesIntro.en: All senses come from one position, behind: behind in time, behind in space, behind in a chase, behind as a copy, and finally standing alone as 'later'.
sensesIntro.cn: 所有义项都来自同一个位置「在后面」：时间在后、空间在后、追赶在后、仿照在后，最后独自站立表示「后来」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the step that comes behind another
core.cn: 核心意象：跟在另一步之后的那一步

branches.en: Behind in time, the most common sense.
branches.cn: 时间上的在后，是最常见的义项。

branches.en: Behind in place or rank.
branches.cn: 位置或等级上的在后。

branches.en: Behind a moving target, which is pursuit.
branches.cn: 跟在移动目标后面，也就是追赶。

branches.en: Behind a model, copying its name or style.
branches.cn: 跟在样板之后，仿其名字或风格。

branches.en: The word standing alone as an adverb.
branches.cn: 这个词独自站立，成为副词。

intro.en: After is a free-standing native word that also works as a combining form in many compounds.
intro.cn: after 是可以独立使用的本族词，也能在许多复合词中充当组合成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; all the pieces are Germanic, including the suffix -wards.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源；所有成分都属于日耳曼语，包括后缀 -wards。

definition_zh: （灾难、战争等的）后果；余波；后续影响
definition_en: the consequences or after effects of a serious event, especially a disaster or a war
core_image: 风暴过去后，仍在水面一圈圈扩散的波纹
scene: 洪水退去后的第三天，街道上堆满淤泥，志愿者挨家挨户清点损失。The town struggled with the aftermath of the flood.
sceneCN: 这里 aftermath 是「（灾难的）后果、余波」（第 1 个义项：重大事件之后留下的影响）；句意为小镇艰难地应对洪水留下的后果。画面中可辨识：淤泥街道、志愿者、受损的房屋。

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，指多次重大事件留下的后果，用于强调不止一场
同族复合词，由 after 与 effect 组成，义为「后效；余波」，与 aftermath 义近但非严格派生

senses.title: The consequences of a disaster or war
senses.definition: the situation that follows a serious event such as a disaster or a war, including damage and suffering
senses.definitionCN: 灾难或战争等重大事件之后出现的局面，包括破坏与苦难
senses.example: The town struggled with the aftermath of the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 小镇艰难地应对洪水留下的后果。
senses.why: The word first named a second crop of grass, and the image of what grows back after cutting became what remains after a disaster.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指第二茬草，割过之后又长出来的意象，转为灾难过后仍然留下的东西。

senses.title: The later effects of any event
senses.definition: the continuing effects or problems caused by an event of any kind
senses.definitionCN: 由任何事件引起的持续影响或问题
senses.example: The resignation was the aftermath of months of disagreement.
senses.exampleCN: 这次辞职是数月分歧留下的结果。
senses.why: Once the word left the field and the battlefield, it could describe the long tail of any event.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词离开田野与战场，它就能描述任何事件拖在后面的长尾。

senses.title: A second crop of grass
senses.definition: a second growth of grass in the same season after the first has been mown, the original sense
senses.definitionCN: 同一季里第一次割过之后又长出的草，是这个词的原义
senses.example: The farmer let the sheep graze on the aftermath.
senses.exampleCN: 农夫让羊在二茬草地上吃草。
senses.why: This is the literal root of the metaphor: mowing is a cutting, and the aftermath is what grows back.
senses.whyCN: 这是比喻的字面根：割草是一种切割，而 aftermath 是割后重新长出来的部分。

intro.en: Aftermath is an agricultural word that became a word for disaster, and the second element is not mathematics.
intro.cn: aftermath 是一个农业词，后来变成灾难用词；它的后半部分与数学毫无关系。

items.en: Mæth meant 'mowing, a cutting of grass', and it survives only inside this compound.
items.cn: mæth 意为「割草、一次收割」，如今只活在这个复合词里。

items.en: Aftermæth meant 'a second mowing', the grass cut after the first harvest.
items.cn: aftermæth 意为「第二次割草」，即第一次收割之后割下的草。

items.en: The word is recorded in the agricultural sense of a second crop of grass.
items.cn: 这个词有记录的最初义项是农学的「二茬草」。

items.en: The figurative sense of consequences grew from the image of what grows back after cutting.
items.cn: 「后果」的比喻义从「割后重新长出」的意象发展而来。

items.en: War and disaster reporting fixed the phrase in the aftermath of, making the word almost inseparable from crisis.
items.cn: 战争与灾难报道固定了 in the aftermath of 这一说法，使这个词几乎与危机不可分割。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built with the same after element; the near-meaning group gathers words for consequences and lingering effects.
note.cn: 形近组收同样由 after 构成的一族词；近义组收表示后果与残留影响的词。

entries.definition: The base preposition and adverb meaning later or behind.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「在……之后；在后面」，是 aftermath 的前半部分。

entries.definition: At a later time, after something has happened.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「之后；后来」，与 aftermath 共享 after 成分。

entries.definition: An effect that continues or appears after the cause has passed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后效；余波」，是 after 与 effect 构成的同族复合词。

entries.definition: A result or effect of an action or event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后果；结果」，最中性，可指好坏两种结果。

entries.definition: An indirect and often unwanted effect that spreads from an event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「间接影响；反响」，强调波及与连锁反应。

entries.definition: The bad results or radioactive dust that follow an explosion or event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「（核爆后的）放射性尘降；不良后果」，语气比 aftermath 更重。

entries.definition: The track left in water by a moving ship, or the aftermath of an event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「尾迹；余波」，与 aftermath 的波纹意象最接近。

normalIntro.en: Aftermath is anchored by its farm origin: after the mowing comes the second growth.
normalIntro.cn: aftermath 可以靠它的农学出身来记：割草之后，又长出第二茬。

normal.en: The math here means mowing, not mathematics, so aftermath is what grows after the cut.
normal.cn: 这里的 math 意为「割草」，不是数学，所以 aftermath 是割过之后长出来的东西。

normal.en: A second crop of grass is the literal sense, and consequences are the figurative one.
normal.cn: 二茬草是字面义，后果是比喻义。

normal.en: In the aftermath of is the fixed phrase you will meet in news writing.
normal.cn: in the aftermath of 是新闻写作里常见的固定说法。

normal.en: Aftereffect is the closest cousin, built with after and effect.
normal.cn: aftereffect 是最接近的同族词，由 after 与 effect 构成。

normal.en: The word almost always follows a disaster, a war, or a crisis.
normal.cn: 这个词几乎总是跟在灾难、战争或危机之后。

abstract.en: Picture a field just mown, with new green shoots pushing through the stubble.
abstract.cn: 想象一片刚割过的田野，新的绿芽从茬口里钻出来。

abstract.en: Think of a flood retreating and leaving a line of mud on every wall.
abstract.cn: 想象洪水退去，在每面墙上留下一条泥线。

abstract.en: See the word as the long shadow an event casts after it has ended.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一个事件结束后投下的长影子。

examples.en: The town struggled with the aftermath of the flood.
examples.cn: 小镇艰难地应对洪水留下的后果。

examples.en: In the aftermath of the war, many families moved abroad.
examples.cn: 战争结束后，许多家庭移居国外。

examples.en: Volunteers carried shovels into the muddy streets.
examples.cn: 志愿者带着铁锹走进满是淤泥的街道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿夫特麦斯」——阿（a）夫（fu）特（te）麦（mai）斯（si），风暴过后还要收拾的一地麦茬。

root: 古英语 aftermæth 由 after「在后」与 mæth「割草」构成，原义为「二茬草」，后来比喻重大事件之后留下的后果。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts in a field, moves to a battlefield, and ends as the general word for whatever an event leaves behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从田野出发，走到战场，最后成为泛指事件遗留之物的词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ripples still spreading after the storm
core.cn: 核心意象：风暴过后仍在扩散的波纹

branches.en: What a disaster leaves behind.
branches.cn: 灾难留下的东西。

branches.en: The long tail of any event.
branches.cn: 任何事件拖在后面的长尾。

branches.en: The literal second crop of grass.
branches.cn: 字面意义上的二茬草。

branches.en: The farm image and the disaster image share one shape.
branches.cn: 农学意象与灾难意象共享同一个形状。

branches.en: Immediate damage and continuing effects.
branches.cn: 眼前的破坏与持续的影响。

intro.en: Aftermath is a compound of two native elements, and its family is a set of similar after- compounds.
intro.cn: aftermath 是两个本族成分构成的复合词，其词族是一组相似的 after 复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source in this compound; both after and math are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词没有拉丁语来源；after 与 math 都属于日耳曼语。

items.meaningCN: 原因过去后仍有的影响

items.meaning: a closing note to a book
a smaller quake after a large one

definition_zh: 下午；午后
definition_en: the part of the day between noon and evening
core_image: 正午之后、黄昏之前的一段斜光
scene: 夏天的院子里，蝉声从树荫里传来，老人搬着藤椅往阴凉处挪。We spent the afternoon reading under the pear tree.
sceneCN: 这里 afternoon 是「下午、午后」（第 1 个义项：正午到傍晚之间的时段）；句意为我们在梨树下读了一下午的书。画面中可辨识：院子、树荫、藤椅。

derivatives.zh: 由复数形式转化而来的副词，义为「每天下午；每逢下午」
复合词，由 mid- 与 afternoon 组成，义为「下午过半时；午后中段」

senses.title: The time between noon and evening
senses.definition: the period of the day from noon until evening
senses.definitionCN: 一天中从正午到傍晚的时段
senses.example: We spent the afternoon reading under the pear tree.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在梨树下读了一下午的书。
senses.why: The word is literally 'after noon', so the boundary of the period is fixed by the sun at its highest point.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面就是「正午之后」，时段的边界由太阳升到最高点的那一刻确定。

senses.title: A period of time in the afternoon
senses.definition: a particular stretch of time in the afternoon, often described by what happens in it
senses.definitionCN: 下午中的某一段时间，常以其间发生的事情来描述
senses.example: It was a lazy afternoon of cards and cold tea.
senses.exampleCN: 那是一个打牌、喝凉茶的慵懒午后。
senses.why: Once the period has a boundary, it can be filled with events, so afternoon also names a whole stretch of experience.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个时段有了边界，就能被事件填满，所以 afternoon 也指一整段经历。

senses.title: Used before another noun
senses.definition: used as a modifier before a noun to mean happening in the afternoon
senses.definitionCN: 用作名词前的修饰语，表示发生在下午
senses.example: The afternoon train was almost empty.
senses.exampleCN: 下午那班火车几乎空着。
senses.why: English often lets a time noun stand before another noun, and here it simply labels when something happens.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让时间名词站在另一个名词前面，这里它只是标明事情发生在下午。

intro.en: Afternoon is a transparent compound: after plus noon, and noon itself comes from a Latin phrase for the ninth hour.
intro.cn: afternoon 是一个透明的复合词：after 加 noon，而 noon 本身来自拉丁语表示「第九个小时」的说法。

items.en: Nona hora meant 'the ninth hour' of the day, roughly three in the afternoon by Roman counting.
items.cn: nona hora 意为一天中的「第九个小时」，按罗马计时大约相当于午后三点。

items.en: English borrowed the church sense of non as the hour of midday prayer, and noon came to mean twelve o'clock.
items.cn: 英语借入 non 的教会义，指正午祈祷的时刻，noon 后来指十二点。

items.en: Afternoon appears as after + noon, naming the hours following midday.
items.cn: afternoon 以 after 加 noon 的形式出现，指正午之后的几个小时。

items.en: The compound settled as a single noun for the whole period before evening.
items.cn: 这个复合词固定为单个名词，指傍晚之前的整个时段。

items.en: Afternoon tea and afternoon nap became fixed phrases of daily routine.
items.cn: afternoon tea 与 afternoon nap 成为日常生活的固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the two halves of the compound; the near-meaning group gathers other parts of the day.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两个组成部分；近义组收一天中的其他时段。

entries.definition: The preposition and adverb meaning later or behind.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「在……之后；在后面」，是 afternoon 的前半部分。

entries.definition: Twelve o'clock in the middle of the day.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正午；中午十二点」，是 afternoon 的后半部分。

entries.definition: The middle of the day, around twelve o'clock.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正午」，指一天的正中，与 noon 义近。

entries.definition: The period between the afternoon and night.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「傍晚；晚上」，是 afternoon 之后的时段。

entries.definition: The time just before night when the light fades.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黄昏；暮色」，指天黑前的短暂时段。

entries.definition: The period from sunrise until noon.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「上午；早晨」，是 afternoon 之前的时段。

normalIntro.en: Afternoon explains itself: it is the time after noon, and the compounds around it are everyday phrases.
normalIntro.cn: afternoon 自己就把意思说了：正午之后的时间，围绕它的复合词也都是日常说法。

normal.en: After plus noon gives the period after twelve, so the spelling tells the meaning.
normal.cn: after 加 noon 就是十二点之后的时段，拼写直接把意思说了出来。

normal.en: Afternoon tea is a fixed British phrase and a strong anchor for the noun.
normal.cn: afternoon tea 是英式固定说法，能牢牢固定这个名词。

normal.en: Mid-afternoon marks the middle of that period, not its beginning.
normal.cn: mid-afternoon 指这个时段的中段，而不是开头。

normal.en: The plural afternoons can become an adverb meaning 'every afternoon'.
normal.cn: 复数 afternoons 可以变成副词，意为「每天下午」。

normal.en: Noon comes from a Latin phrase for the ninth hour, so the word carries a clock inside it.
normal.cn: noon 来自拉丁语「第九个小时」的说法，所以这个词里藏着一只钟。

abstract.en: Picture the sun past its highest point, throwing long shadows across a courtyard.
abstract.cn: 想象太阳越过最高点，把长长的影子投在院子里。

abstract.en: Think of the quiet hour when shops are open but the day already feels used.
abstract.cn: 想象那段安静的时光：店铺还开着，但一天已经像被用掉了一半。

abstract.en: See the word as a bridge between lunch and sunset.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成午饭与日落之间的一座桥。

examples.en: We spent the afternoon reading under the pear tree.
examples.cn: 我们在梨树下读了一下午的书。

examples.en: The afternoon train was almost empty.
examples.cn: 下午那班火车几乎空着。

examples.en: The cicadas kept singing in the shade.
examples.cn: 蝉在树荫里一直叫个不停。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿夫特努恩」——阿（a）夫（fu）特（te）努（nu）恩（en），正午之后的那段时光。

root: 由 after「在……之后」与 noon「正午」复合而成；noon 来自拉丁语 nona hora「第九个小时」，经教会用语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: One fixed period of the clock expands into a stretch of experience, then turns into a modifier before another noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个固定的时钟时段扩展为一段经历，再转为另一个名词前的修饰语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: slanted light after the sun has passed its peak
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳越过最高点之后的斜光

branches.en: The clock period from noon to evening.
branches.cn: 从正午到傍晚的时钟时段。

branches.en: That period filled with particular events.
branches.cn: 被具体事件填满的那段时光。

branches.en: The same word used as a modifier.
branches.cn: 同一个词用作修饰语。

branches.en: The period itself and anything happening in it.
branches.cn: 时段本身与发生在其间的事物。

branches.en: A remembered afternoon and an afternoon train.
branches.cn: 一段被记住的午后与一班下午的火车。

intro.en: Afternoon is a compound of two native words, and its parts reappear in many time expressions.
intro.cn: afternoon 由两个本族词复合而成，它的组成部分在许多时间表达里反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Noon traces to Latin nona hora, but the compound itself was built inside English.
latinIntro.cn: noon 可追到拉丁语 nona hora，但这个复合词本身是在英语内部构成的。

items.meaning: a short sleep in the afternoon
the later part of the afternoon

latinEntries.example: Nona hora lies behind noon.
latinEntries.exampleCN: nona hora 是 noon 的来源。

definition_zh: 之后；后来；随后
definition_en: at a later time, after an event has happened
core_image: 一件事结束之后才开始的那段时间
scene: 葬礼结束，亲友们在教堂门口低声交谈，天色渐渐暗下来。Shortly afterwards, the family gathered at the old house.
sceneCN: 这里 afterwards 是「之后、随后」（第 1 个义项：在某事发生以后的时间里）；句意为不久之后，家人聚到了那栋老房子里。画面中可辨识：教堂门口、低声交谈的亲友、渐暗的天色。

derivatives.zh: 美式拼写形式，义同「之后；后来」
本词去掉 -wards 后的基础词，义为「在……之后；在后面」

senses.title: At a later time
senses.definition: at a time later than an event that has already happened
senses.definitionCN: 在已经发生的事件之后的时间里
senses.example: Shortly afterwards, the family gathered at the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 不久之后，家人聚到了那栋老房子里。
senses.why: The word is after plus a directional ending, so it points from an event toward the time beyond it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 after 加一个方向词尾，从某个事件指向它之后的时间。

senses.title: Next in sequence
senses.definition: next in order or sequence, especially in a narrative
senses.definitionCN: 在顺序或叙述中紧接着发生
senses.example: The lights went out; afterwards there was only silence.
senses.exampleCN: 灯灭了；随后只剩一片寂静。
senses.why: Sequence is time made orderly, so the same adverb can mark the next step in a story.
senses.whyCN: 顺序是被整理过的时间，所以同一个副词也能标记故事里的下一步。

senses.title: Looking back after the event
senses.definition: when considered in retrospect, after the event is over
senses.definitionCN: 在事情结束之后回看的视角
senses.example: Afterwards she could not explain why she had agreed.
senses.exampleCN: 事后她说不清自己当时为什么答应了。
senses.why: Hindsight places the speaker after the event, and afterwards names that backward-looking position.
senses.whyCN: 事后之明把说话者放在事件之后，afterwards 指的就是这个回望的位置。

intro.en: Afterwards is after fitted with a directional ending, and its American twin drops the s.
intro.cn: afterwards 是 after 加上方向词尾，它的美式双胞胎则去掉了 s。

items.en: Æfter meant 'after, behind, later', and it is the base of the whole family.
items.cn: æfter 意为「在后、后来」，是整个词族的基础。

items.en: The directional element -weard meant 'toward', and it also survives in toward and forward.
items.cn: 方向成分 -weard 意为「朝向」，也保留在 toward 与 forward 里。

items.en: Afterward combined the two into an adverb pointing toward a later time.
items.cn: afterward 把两者结合成指向较晚时间的副词。

items.en: The form afterwards added a plural-looking -s, which became standard in British usage.
items.cn: afterwards 加了一个看似复数的 -s，这一形式在英式用法中成为标准。

items.en: Both afterwards and afterward are accepted, with regional preferences in British and American writing.
items.cn: afterwards 与 afterward 都被接受，英式与美式写作各有偏好。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's variants and its base; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs for later time.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的变体与基础词；近义组收表示较晚时间的副词。

entries.definition: The American spelling, meaning at a later time.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「之后；后来」，是 afterwards 的美式拼写。

entries.definition: The preposition and adverb meaning later or behind.
entries.definitionCN: 介词与副词，义为「在……之后；在后面」，是 afterwards 的基础词。

entries.definition: The consequences left by a serious event.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「后果；余波」，与 afterwards 共享 after 成分。

entries.definition: At a time after the present or after a stated point.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「后来；较晚地」，最通用，语气比 afterwards 轻。

entries.definition: After a particular event, used in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「随后；接着」，比 afterwards 正式得多。

entries.definition: After that point in time, used in formal or legal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「此后；在那之后」，多见于正式或法律文本。

entries.definition: In the end, after a long time or series of events.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「最终」，强调经过一段过程后的结果，而非紧接其后。

normalIntro.en: Afterwards is after plus a direction, and its s is a British habit rather than a plural.
normalIntro.cn: afterwards 是 after 加方向成分，词尾的 s 是英式习惯，而不是复数。

normal.en: After points to what comes next, and -wards points toward it, so the word means 'toward later'.
normal.cn: after 指向后面，-wards 朝那个方向，所以这个词意为「朝较晚的时候」。

normal.en: Afterward is the American form and afterwards is the British one.
normal.cn: afterward 是美式形式，afterwards 是英式形式。

normal.en: Shortly afterwards is the phrase you will hear most often.
normal.cn: shortly afterwards 是最常听到的搭配。

normal.en: Thereafter is its formal cousin, common in legal writing.
normal.cn: thereafter 是它正式的近亲，常见于法律文本。

normal.en: The s at the end is not a plural; the word is an adverb.
normal.cn: 词尾的 s 不是复数，这个词是副词。

abstract.en: Picture a door closing and a second door opening a moment later.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门关上，片刻之后另一扇门打开。

abstract.en: Think of a photograph taken just after everyone has left the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一张在所有人离开房间之后才拍下的照片。

abstract.en: See time as a road: afterwards is the stretch you can only describe once you have passed it.
abstract.cn: 把时间看成一条路：afterwards 是你走过之后才能描述的那一段。

examples.en: Shortly afterwards, the family gathered at the old house.
examples.cn: 不久之后，家人聚到了那栋老房子里。

examples.en: The lights went out; afterwards there was only silence.
examples.cn: 灯灭了；随后只剩一片寂静。

examples.en: The church bells rang twice that evening.
examples.cn: 那天傍晚教堂的钟响了两次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿夫特沃兹」——阿（a）夫（fu）特（te）沃（wo）兹（zi），一件事过后才发生的另一个时刻。

root: 由 after「在后」加方向成分 -wards「朝……方向」构成；after 来自古英语 æfter，-wards 来自 -weard「朝向」。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb points forward from an event, then marks the next item in a story, and finally names the position of hindsight.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词从事件向前指，随后标记故事里的下一项，最后指事后回望的位置。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the time that opens after a door closes
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇门关上之后展开的时间

branches.en: A later time after an event.
branches.cn: 事件之后的较晚时间。

branches.en: The next item in a narrative order.
branches.cn: 叙述顺序中的下一项。

branches.en: The position from which one looks back.
branches.cn: 回望时所站的位置。

branches.en: Later time and next step are the same arrow.
branches.cn: 较晚的时间与下一步是同一支箭。

branches.en: What happened later and what it looks like now.
branches.cn: 后来发生的事与它如今的样子。

intro.en: Afterwards is a native base plus a native directional suffix, so its parts are best learned together with after.
intro.cn: afterwards 是本族词基加本族方向后缀，最好和 after 一起记它的组成部分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source in this adverb; both parts are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个副词没有拉丁语来源；两个部分都属于日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 再次；又；重新；此外
definition_en: one more time; back to a former state; used to add a further point
core_image: 把同一个动作再做一遍，像回到起点重走
scene: 雨停了一会儿，屋檐的水珠还没落尽，天空又暗了下来。The rain started again before the roof had dried.
sceneCN: 这里 again 是「再次、又」（第 1 个义项：同一动作再发生一次）；句意为屋顶还没干，雨又下了起来。画面中可辨识：屋檐水珠、暗下来的天空、湿漉漉的屋顶。

derivatives.zh: again 的古体拼写变体，义同「再次」，多见于早期文本
固定短语，由 once 与 again 组成，义为「再一次」

senses.title: One more time
senses.definition: one more time, when something happens another time
senses.definitionCN: 某件事再发生一次
senses.example: The rain started again before the roof had dried.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶还没干，雨又下了起来。
senses.why: The word first meant 'toward, against', and the idea of returning to the same point produced 'one more time'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初意为「朝向、对着」，「回到同一点」的想法后来生出「再一次」。

senses.title: Back to a former state
senses.definition: back to a previous good or normal state, as in well again or together again
senses.definitionCN: 回到先前良好或正常的状态，如 well again 或 together again
senses.example: After a week in bed, he was well again.
senses.exampleCN: 卧床一周之后，他又恢复了健康。
senses.why: If an action can be repeated, a state can be recovered, so again also means back where you were.
senses.whyCN: 如果动作可以重复，状态也可以恢复，所以 again 也指回到原来的位置。

senses.title: In addition, moreover
senses.definition: used to introduce a further point or a second consideration
senses.definitionCN: 用来引出另一个论点或第二层考虑
senses.example: Again, the cost is not the only problem.
senses.exampleCN: 再说，成本并不是唯一的问题。
senses.why: A second point is another turn of the same argument, so the repetition word became an addition word.
senses.whyCN: 第二个论点是对同一论证的再一次转回，于是这个表示重复的词也成了补充词。

senses.title: Please say that again
senses.definition: used in speech to ask someone to repeat what they have just said
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来请对方把刚说的话再说一次
senses.example: Come again? I did not catch the name.
senses.exampleCN: 请再说一遍？我没听清那个名字。
senses.why: Asking for a repeat is the most literal social use of the word: say the same thing one more time.
senses.whyCN: 请求重复是这个词最字面的社交用法：把同一句话再说一次。

intro.en: Again and against are doublets from the same Old English root, and 'again' grew out of the idea of turning back.
intro.cn: again 与 against 是同出古英语同一词根的双形式，again 从「转回」的想法生长出来。

items.en: Gegn meant 'against, toward, opposite', and it underlies both again and against.
items.cn: gegn 意为「对着、朝向、相反」，是 again 与 against 共同的底层形式。

items.en: The phrase on gegn meant 'toward, in return, opposite', and it developed in two directions.
items.cn: 短语 on gegn 意为「朝向、作为回报、相对」，后来朝两个方向发展。

items.en: Again took the sense of 'in return, once more', while against kept the sense of opposition.
items.cn: again 取得「作为回报、再一次」的意思，against 则保留「反对」的意思。

items.en: Again is recorded with the modern sense of another time.
items.cn: again 在十四世纪已有「又一次」的现代义记录。

items.en: The discourse sense 'moreover' and the spoken Come again? developed in later usage.
items.cn: 语篇中的「此外」义与口语中的 Come again? 在更晚的用法里发展出来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's doublet and a spelling variant; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of repetition and addition.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的同源双形式与一个拼写变体；近义组收表示重复与补充的副词。

entries.definition: In opposition to, or touching something for support.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「反对；靠着」，与 again 同出古英语 gegn，是同一词根的另一支。

entries.definition: An archaic spelling variant of again.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，again 的古体拼写变体，义同「再次」。

entries.definition: To deny or contradict something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「否认；反驳」，由 gegn 与 say 构成，与 again 同源。

entries.definition: Once more, in a fresh way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「重新；再一次」，比 again 更书面，强调从头开始。

entries.definition: Many times, one after another.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「反复地；多次」，强调次数多。

entries.definition: One additional time.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「再一次」，与 again 基本同义，语气更完整。

entries.definition: In addition to what has been said.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「此外；而且」，对应义项三，但正式得多。

normalIntro.en: Again is held by its doublet against and by the phrase once again.
normalIntro.cn: again 可以靠它与 against 的双形式关系，以及 once again 这个说法来记。

normal.en: Again and against come from the same root: one turned toward repetition, the other toward opposition.
normal.cn: again 与 against 同出一根：一个转向重复，一个转向反对。

normal.en: Once again is the phrase that fixes the 'one more time' sense.
normal.cn: once again 这个说法固定了「再一次」的意思。

normal.en: Again and again means many times, and time and again means the same.
normal.cn: again and again 表示一次又一次，time and again 意思相同。

normal.en: Well again means back to health, not a second illness.
normal.cn: well again 指恢复健康，而不是第二次生病。

normal.en: Come again? is a polite spoken way to ask for a repeat.
normal.cn: Come again? 是口语里礼貌地请求重复的说法。

abstract.en: Picture a record needle returning to the start of the same groove.
abstract.cn: 想象唱针回到同一道纹路的起点。

abstract.en: Think of a wave that comes back to the shore after every pull.
abstract.cn: 想象海浪每次退去之后又回到岸边。

abstract.en: See the word as a loop: the same point, reached from the same direction.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一个环：从同一方向到达同一个点。

examples.en: The rain started again before the roof had dried.
examples.cn: 屋顶还没干，雨又下了起来。

examples.en: After a week in bed, he was well again.
examples.cn: 卧床一周之后，他又恢复了健康。

examples.en: The gutter dripped long after the clouds had passed.
examples.cn: 云过去很久了，屋檐还在滴水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿根」——阿（a）根（gen），回到根上，从头再来一遍。

root: 古英语 gegn「对着、朝向」派生 on gegn，后分化为 again「再一次」与 against「反对」两个形式。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a return to the same point, then covers recovery, a second argument, and a request to repeat.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「回到同一点」出发，随后覆盖恢复、第二个论点与请求重复。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a loop returning to the same starting point
core.cn: 核心意象：回到同一出发点的环

branches.en: The same action done one more time.
branches.cn: 同一动作再做一次。

branches.en: A former state recovered.
branches.cn: 恢复先前的状态。

branches.en: A further point added to the argument.
branches.cn: 给论证再加一个论点。

branches.en: A request to repeat what was said.
branches.cn: 请求把说过的话再说一遍。

branches.en: Repeating an act and returning to a state.
branches.cn: 重复动作与回到状态。

intro.en: Again has no productive affixes of its own, so its construction is best shown through the doublet against and its fixed phrases.
intro.cn: again 自身没有能产的词缀，所以它的构词最好通过同源双形式 against 与固定短语来展示。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the root gegn is Germanic and survives mainly in these set forms.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源；词根 gegn 属于日耳曼语，主要活在这些固定形式里。

items.exampleCN: 请再说一遍；请再说一次

definition_zh: 反对；逆着；靠着；防备；与……相比
definition_en: in opposition to; in the opposite direction to; touching something for support; in preparation for; compared with
core_image: 身体或立场顶在某个东西的对面
scene: 风从山口灌进来，行人把身体前倾，几乎顶着风一步步往前走。They walked against the wind along the empty road.
sceneCN: 这里 against 是「逆着、顶着」（第 2 个义项：与风向相反）；句意为他们沿着空旷的道路逆风而行。画面中可辨识：山口、前倾的行人、空旷的道路。

pos.zh: 反对；逆着；靠着；防备；与……相比

derivatives.zh: 与本词同出古英语 gegn 的双形式，义为「再次」，词义已分化
固定短语，义为「违法」，是本词最常见的搭配之一

senses.title: In opposition to
senses.definition: in opposition to a person, plan, rule, or idea
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某计划、某规则或某想法持反对立场
senses.example: Most residents voted against the new road.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数居民投票反对这条新路。
senses.why: The root meant 'opposite', and opposition is the clearest survival of that earliest sense.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「相对」，反对义是这一最早含义最清楚的留存。

senses.title: In the opposite direction
senses.definition: in the opposite direction to a force such as wind or current
senses.definitionCN: 与风、水流等力量的方向相反
senses.example: They walked against the wind along the empty road.
senses.exampleCN: 他们沿着空旷的道路逆风而行。
senses.why: Two forces face each other, and one moves into the other, which is the physical shape of against.
senses.whyCN: 两股力量面对面，其中一方顶向另一方，这就是 against 的物理形状。

senses.title: Touching for support
senses.definition: touching or pressing on something, often for support or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 接触或压在某物上，常为了支撑或施压
senses.example: She leaned against the wall and closed her eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠在墙上，闭上了眼睛。
senses.why: Support comes from contact, so the opposite-facing word also covers bodies pressed together.
senses.whyCN: 支撑来自接触，所以这个表示「相对」的词也覆盖身体相互抵靠的情形。

senses.title: As protection from
senses.definition: in preparation for or as protection from something harmful
senses.definitionCN: 为有害之物做准备，或作为对它的防护
senses.example: The vaccine protects children against measles.
senses.exampleCN: 这种疫苗保护儿童不得麻疹。
senses.why: To stand against a danger is to face it prepared, so opposition becomes defence.
senses.whyCN: 站在危险对面就是面对它并做好准备，于是反对变成了防备。

senses.title: Compared with
senses.definition: used to compare one thing with another, or to set something in front of a background
senses.definitionCN: 用于把一物与另一物比较，或把某物置于背景之前
senses.example: Against last year's figures, the decline looks small.
senses.exampleCN: 与去年的数字相比，这次下降显得很小。
senses.why: Comparison places one thing opposite another so the eye can measure the difference.
senses.whyCN: 比较把一物放在另一物的对面，让眼睛能够衡量差异。

intro.en: Against and again are twins from one Old English root meaning 'toward, opposite'.
intro.cn: against 与 again 是同出古英语一个词根的双胞胎，原义为「朝向、相对」。

items.en: Gegn meant 'against, toward, opposite', and it is the shared root of both words.
items.cn: gegn 意为「对着、朝向、相反」，是两个词共同的词根。

items.en: The fuller form ongegn meant 'toward, opposite, in return'.
items.cn: 更完整的形式 ongegn 意为「朝向、相对、作为回报」。

items.en: The form against added a final -st and specialized in the sense of opposition and contact.
items.cn: against 加上词尾 -st，并专门发展出反对与接触的含义。

items.en: The preposition is recorded with senses of opposition, direction, and support.
items.cn: 这个介词在十四世纪已有反对、方向与支撑等义项的记录。

items.en: The comparative sense 'against a background' became common in modern descriptive writing.
items.cn: 「以……为背景」的比较义在现代描写性写作中变得常见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the word's doublet and other forms from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers expressions of opposition and contact.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的同源双形式与同一词根的其他形式；近义组收表示反对与接触的说法。

entries.definition: One more time; back to a former state.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「再次；重新」，与 against 同出古英语 gegn，词义已分化。

entries.definition: To deny or contradict something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「否认；反驳」，由 gegn 与 say 构成，与 against 同源。

entries.definition: In the middle of a group; a variant of among.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之中」，是 among 的变体；词尾与 against 相似，词源不同。

entries.definition: Disagreeing with or resisting something.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「反对」，与义项一相近，语气更明确。

entries.definition: Against, especially in a contest or comparison.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「对；与……相对」，多用于比赛或对比，源自拉丁语。

entries.definition: In opposition to a rule, expectation, or belief.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「与……相反」，多用于规则或预期。

entries.definition: On or touching something, sometimes suggesting pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「在……之上；靠着」，与义项三的接触义相近。

normalIntro.en: Against is the opposition twin of again, and its senses all keep two things facing each other.
normalIntro.cn: against 是 again 的「对立」双胞胎，它的所有义项都保留两物相对的结构。

normal.en: Again and against share one root: one turns back, the other turns to face.
normal.cn: again 与 against 共享一个词根：一个转回，一个转过去面对。

normal.en: Against the wind is the physical picture behind the preposition.
normal.cn: against the wind 是这个词背后的物理画面。

normal.en: Lean against keeps the contact sense, where one body supports another.
normal.cn: lean against 保留接触义：一个身体支撑另一个。

normal.en: Protect against turns opposition into defence.
normal.cn: protect against 把「相对」转成「防备」。

normal.en: Against a background places one thing in front of another for comparison.
normal.cn: against a background 把一物放在另一物前面以便比较。

abstract.en: Picture two doors pressed back to back, neither able to close.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇门背对背顶住，谁也关不上。

abstract.en: Think of a swimmer cutting into a current that keeps pushing back.
abstract.cn: 想象游泳者切进一股不断推回来的水流。

abstract.en: See the word as a wall you can lean on or a wall you argue with.
abstract.cn: 把这个词看成一堵可以靠着的墙，或一堵你要与之争辩的墙。

examples.en: They walked against the wind along the empty road.
examples.cn: 他们沿着空旷的道路逆风而行。

examples.en: She leaned against the wall and closed her eyes.
examples.cn: 她靠在墙上，闭上了眼睛。

examples.en: The road was empty except for a single cart.
examples.cn: 除了辆独轮车，路上空无一人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿根斯特」——阿（a）根（gen）斯（si）特（te），身体顶在对面，表示反对或逆着。

root: 古英语 gegn「对着、朝向」派生出 ongegn，后加词尾 -st 固定为 against；与 again 同源，一支转向「反对」，一支转向「再次」。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense places two things face to face: a vote and a plan, a walker and the wind, a body and a wall, a child and a disease, a figure and its background.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都把两样东西面对面放置：选票与计划、行人与风、身体与墙、孩子与疾病、数字与背景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things pressed face to face
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西面对面顶住

branches.en: A stance set opposite another.
branches.cn: 与另一方相对的立场。

branches.en: Movement into an opposing force.
branches.cn: 顶向相反力量的运动。

branches.en: Two surfaces in contact for support.
branches.cn: 两个表面接触以取得支撑。

branches.en: Facing a danger with protection ready.
branches.cn: 面对危险并做好防护。

branches.en: One thing set opposite another to be measured.
branches.cn: 把一物放在另一物对面以便衡量。

intro.en: Against is a fossilized preposition, so its construction is shown through the shared root and its fixed phrases.
intro.cn: against 是凝固的介词，所以它的构词通过共同词根与固定短语来展示。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the root gegn is Germanic and the -st ending is adverbial.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语来源；词根 gegn 属于日耳曼语，-st 是副词性词尾。
